title: Carly Simon seemingly takes aim at ex James Taylor on new album as she sings, 'Maybe I never loved you'
summary: Carly Simon's new album, "Comes in Waves," features a track that appears aimed at ex-husband James Taylor, questioning whether their love ever existed.
story: Fox News Flash top entertainment and celebrity headlines are here.
Carly Simon appears to take aim at ex-husband James Taylor with a five-word bombshell: "Maybe I never loved you."
The Grammy-winning singer seems to turn the wreckage of their decade-long marriage into a song on her new album, "Comes in Waves."
"Maybe I never loved you / But anyway, I thought I did," Simon sings on the album’s second track. "I married you, we had a kid / That counts for something."
‘YOU’RE SO VAIN’ SINGER CARLY SIMON SAYS PARKINSON’S AND CANCER DIAGNOSES KEPT HER FROM PUBLIC EYE
James Taylor and Carly Simon circa 1979 in New York City. (Robin Platzer/Images/Getty Images)
She immediately undercuts her own certainty, wondering whether she did love her former husband — and whether he ever truly loved her.
"Maybe I never loved you / Yes, and maybe I did," she sings. "And maybe you never loved me / Although God knows, you said you did."
Taylor is never identified by name.
Simon was married to the "Fire and Rain" singer from 1972 to 1983. Their relationship was rocky and remained in the public eye for decades.
"You came for me those times I hid / I’m so glad you did that," she sings. "And maybe it’s wrong to wonder how everything kind became forbidden."
Carly Simon returns after an 18-year hiatus with song lyrics seemingly directed at her ex, James Taylor. (Richard E. Aaron/Redferns)
The song eventually concludes with what sounds like a final attempt at closure.
"And maybe it’s best to bury whatever it was we had our fill of," she sings. "Maybe I never loved you / Maybe I always will."
Fox News Digital has reached out to both Simon and Taylor for comment.
In a 2015 interview with People, Simon said she and Taylor had not spoken in more than a decade.
"I still want to heal him. I still want to make him all right," she said. "And I love him so much."
Simon said Taylor's treatment of her had been deeply painful, but writing her memoir helped her understand something about herself and about unrequited love.
IN MEMOIR, CARLY SIMON REVEALS SHE USED 'SPANISH WITCH DOCTOR' TO HELP SAVE HER MARRIAGE
Carly Simon sings, "Maybe I never loved you / Maybe I always will" in her new song, "Maybe I Never Loved You" from her latest album. (Bettmann)

"My incredible loyalty to him, in spite of the fact that he has treated me without any regard, has been so painful to me for so long," she told the outlet. "But, through the course of writing the book, I really started to understand that I could love and not be loved. And that was the big realization for me, that it doesn’t have to be a two-way street."
The deeply personal album arrives as Simon has also been navigating significant health challenges away from the spotlight.
The "You’re So Vain" singer has Parkinson’s disease and recently had surgery for basal cell carcinoma, a form of skin cancer.
Simon explained to People why she had largely stayed out of the public eye.
Carly Simon appears to address her marriage and divorce from James Taylor on her new album, "Comes in Waves." (Clint Spaulding/WWD/Penske Media via Getty Images)
"It has taken me some time to understand the diagnosis, to adjust to it, and to decide how much I wanted to say about it publicly," the 83-year-old told the outlet in a statement published July 27.

"Parkinson's is different for everyone, and it can be unpredictable," she continued. "Some days I'm so tired I can't get the day moving at all. On others, it gives me a little more room to move, think, work and feel like myself."

Her comments offer a rare glimpse into what the legendary singer has been experiencing privately while continuing to create music.
Her latest project, "Comes in Waves," marks the end of an 18-year hiatus from releasing original music, and she's looking squarely at the past while confronting the realities of the present.
Simon and Taylor were one of music's ultimate power couples of the 1970s.
Their romance moved fast. Simon said she went to Taylor's dressing room at New York's Carnegie Hall in 1971 after seeing him perform.
On July 27, 2026, Carly Simon told People magazine in a statement she has Parkinson’s disease. (Jack Mitchell/Getty Images)

"I have a wonderful history with Carnegie Hall," she said previously in a Harper’s Bazaar interview. "I met James there that same year when I went to his dressing room to say hello, and he invited himself to my home for a late-night lunch that expanded into a life together."
By the following year, they were married.
Their wedding took place Nov. 3, 1972, in a small ceremony at Simon's New York home.

But the marriage didn't last.
The couple separated in 1981, and their divorce was finalized in 1983. They share two children, Sally Taylor and Ben Taylor.
Behind the scenes, their marriage was unraveling as Taylor struggled with drug addiction. Both Simon and Taylor have acknowledged infidelity during their marriage.
Simon later described their relationship in her 2015 memoir, "Boys in the Trees," as "far from the idyllic one that the general public reads about."
Simon recently underwent surgery for basal cell carcinoma, a form of skin cancer. (Richard E. Aaron/Redferns)
She had an even harsher description of their relationship.
"Our love became bipolar, switching from love to hate, lust to loathing, and back again, sometimes within a day," Simon wrote.
Taylor has also acknowledged how deeply his addiction damaged his relationships.
"You could fall in love, but if one of the people is addicted, it’s not going to work," he told Parade. "The whole person is simply not available."

title: Meghan Markle, Prince Harry's box-office flop shows 'infamy' doesn't equal success: expert
summary: Prince Harry and Meghan Markle's Girl Scouts documentary opened in 446 theaters, but royal experts question whether Sussex star power sells tickets.
story: Catherine Mayer, author of "Divide & Rule," explains why Prince Harry and Meghan Markle's departure from royal life dealt a lasting blow to the monarchy and its connection with younger audiences.

Though Prince Harry and Meghan Markle may still dominate headlines, their latest Hollywood venture is raising questions about whether the Duke and Duchess of Sussex's names can convert all that attention into paying customers.

Following the recent release of "Cookie Queens," a documentary executive produced by the couple through Archewell Productions that follows four Girl Scouts navigating the highly competitive world of cookie sales while examining ambition, leadership and adolescence, the movie's opening weekend failed to produce strong box-office numbers.

"Cookie Queens" earned approximately $354,000 from 446 theaters, according to reported box-office figures. The documentary was beaten by "CatVideoFest 2026," a compilation of viral internet cat videos that earned approximately $569,000 despite playing on just 255 screens.
PRINCE HARRY, MEGHAN MARKLE’S HOLLYWOOD DREAMS HIT WALL AS EXPERT WARNS OF ‘TOXIC BRAND’ STIGMA
Prince Harry and Meghan Markle executive produced a new documentary, "Cookie Queens," through Archewell Productions.  (The David Foster Foundation via Getty Images)
Fox News Digital reached out to Archewell for comment.
The result has royal experts questioning whether Harry and Meghan's ability to dominate the news cycle still carries the same weight it once did.

"Harry and Meghan remain extraordinarily effective at generating headlines, but headlines and paying customers are two very different things," royal commentator Kinsey Schofield, host of YouTube's "Kinsey Schofield Unfiltered," told Fox News Digital.
"There was a period when simply attaching their names to something guaranteed enormous curiosity. I’m not convinced that’s true anymore."
MARTHA STEWART QUESTIONS MEGHAN MARKLE’S HOMEMAKING CREDENTIALS WITH BLUNT CAREER ASSESSMENT

"And there’s no getting around the optics of finishing five places behind a 70-minute compilation of internet cat videos. Hollywood can forgive a lot, but being beaten by ‘CatVideoFest’ is the sort of indignity that writes its own punchline."

Alysa Nahmias and Meghan Markle, Duchess of Sussex, attend a special screening of Roadside Attractions' "Cookie Queens" at AMC The Grove 14 in Los Angeles on July 28, 2026. (Roadside Attractions via Getty Images)
The Duchess of Sussex personally promoted the documentary ahead of its theatrical debut, discussing the movie and her own childhood experience as a Girl Scout.
Schofield said that involvement makes the opening numbers particularly noteworthy.

"Meghan certainly has enormous name recognition, but I think, at this stage, it’s fair to ask how much of that is fame and how much is infamy," she said. "There’s a significant difference commercially.

"People may click on a Meghan Markle headline because they’re fascinated by her or irritated by her. That doesn’t mean they’re going to buy a movie ticket because her name is attached to the project. ‘Cookie Queens’ gives us another interesting data point on that distinction."
MEGHAN MARKLE'S SHOW EMMY NOMINATION 'SOMEWHAT BAFFLING' DUE TO LACKLUSTER RATINGS: EXPERT

British royals expert Hilary Fordwich shared the same sentiment in that the performance raises questions about the couple's ability to attract audiences when their projects are not centered on the royal family.

"Harry and Meghan remain extraordinarily effective at generating headlines, but headlines and paying customers are two very different things," royal commentator Kinsey Schofield told Fox News Digital. (Chris Jackson/Pool/Getty Images)

"The extremely underwhelming box office is a clear indication that, yet again, unless they are bashing the royals and sharing inside stories, secrets and betraying the privacy of the family, there isn’t much they have that is at all in demand nor popular," Fordwich told Fox News Digital.
"Meghan certainly doesn’t have the commercial pull she has so desired."
Fordwich argued the couple now face increased pressure to demonstrate they can produce a genuine mainstream hit.
OPRAH WINFREY SPARKS FRESH BACKLASH AFTER SHE REVISITS PRINCE HARRY AND MEGHAN MARKLE BOMBSHELL INTERVIEW
That question has followed the Sussexes throughout their post-royal entertainment career.

After stepping back from royal duties in 2020 and relocating to California, Harry and Meghan signed major deals in Hollywood. Their Netflix docuseries, "Harry & Meghan," released in 2022, generated enormous attention by focusing heavily on the couple's departure from royal life and their relationship with the monarchy.
The couple stepped back from royal duties in 2020.  (Matt Dunham/WPA Pool/Getty Images)
Harry's 2023 memoir, "Spare," similarly produced worldwide headlines with its claims about life inside the royal family.
Royal expert Richard Fitzwilliams told Fox News Digital those projects remain the couple's most significant attention grabbers.

"We all know their huge hits were the three infamous betrayals of the royal family, on Oprah, the Netflix series ‘Harry & Meghan’ and Harry’s memoir ‘Spare,’" Fitzwilliams said. "What is undoubted is the publicity that accompanies everything they do."
WATCH: PRINCE HARRY AND MEGHAN MARKLE'S EXIT HURT THE MONARCHY: AUTHOR
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

"The world knows who they are but isn't curious enough to tune in and watch Meghan's ghastly series 'With Love, Meghan,' their series on the Invictus Games, 'Polo' or, it seems, 'Cookie Queens.' Reports vary on the exact level of success or failure of Meghan's brand As Ever, but the jam, flower sprinkles and scented candles have become a bit of a joke.
"So, it’s all about buzz and nothing else, save their link with real royalty."
Since relocating to California, both Harry and Meghan have been involved in multiple Hollywood projects.  (Chris Jackson/Getty Images)

Still, for Schofield, the numbers connected to "Cookie Queens" add to a broader question involving Archewell as Harry and Meghan move further away from the royal family drama and focus more on their American ventures.
"Harry and Meghan are a fascinating case study in the difference between attention and commercial influence," Schofield said.
PRINCE HARRY LONGS FOR HIS OLD ROYAL LIFE AS AMERICA ISN'T WHAT HE EXPECTED, EXPERTS SAY

"Infamy can be extremely valuable to newspapers, television shows and social media platforms because people will click, argue and engage. Monetizing that attention yourself is a completely different challenge.
"People want to consume content about Harry and Meghan," she added, "but are they equally interested in consuming content from Harry and Meghan?"
A royal expert told Fox News Digital the curiosity surrounding them was "enormous" when they first moved to California.  (Chris Jackson)
Schofield said Hollywood's expectations have changed considerably since the couple first arrived in California.

"When Harry and Meghan first arrived in California, they were the story," she said. "Hollywood was essentially buying access to two people who had just walked away from the royal family, and the curiosity surrounding them was enormous.
"Six years later, the novelty has diminished. The questions are much more conventional now: What can you produce? What can you sell? Can you build an audience around something that isn’t royal drama?
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
"They’ve had the deals, resources and access," she continued. "At this stage, tangible results matter."
Schofield believes the couple's future standing in Hollywood may depend less on announcements and more on execution.
The couple share two children together.  (Angela Weiss)

"Hollywood is full of projects that die in development, so, individually, none of those are necessarily remarkable," she said. "But when you establish a pattern of big announcements without finished products, you risk damaging your credibility.
"You cannot build a serious production reputation on press releases and announcements," Schofield added.
And that, she said, is why even a relatively small documentary such as "Cookie Queens" matters.
"When a project does reach audiences, its performance becomes part of the résumé," Schofield said.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
"Being beaten at the box office by ‘CatVideoFest’ is funny, but against this larger backdrop, it makes the need for a genuine success that much more urgent."

Christina Dugan Ramirez is an entertainment journalist with more than 15 years of experience, including a decade at PEOPLE writing high-profile cover stories, covering Hollywood's biggest events, and interviewing many of the industry's most influential stars before joining Fox News Digital in 2024.

title: Kelly Osbourne blasts Dee Snider as 'spectacularly classless' for claiming Ozzy didn’t write his own songs
summary: Kelly Osbourne called Dee Snider's claims about her father's songwriting "spectacularly classless," igniting a fierce debate over Ozzy Osbourne's legacy.
story: Piers Morgan remembers Ozzy Osbourne after the heavy metal legend was laid to rest in his hometown of Birmingham, England.
Kelly Osbourne and Twisted Sister frontman Dee Snider are going head-to-head after the retired musician claimed Ozzy Osbourne "always" had other people write his songs for him.

Earlier this week, Snider wrote on X, "Ozzy always had bass players write his lyrics." He went on to claim that bassist Bob Daisley and Motörhead frontman Lemmy Kilmister were frequent writers of Ozzy's music, and that Geezer Butler "wrote ALL of @BlackSabbath lyrics."

According to Daisley's website, he claimed to have written the majority of the songs for Ozzy's first five solo albums. Daisley is credited as a songwriter on "Blizzard of Ozz" and "No Rest for the Wicked." During Ozzy's time with Black Sabbath, Butler was widely credited as the main lyricist for the band.
Snider's comments prompted a sharp response from Ozzy's daughter via her Instagram Stories Friday.
KELLY OSBOURNE DEMANDS CHILD SUPPORT AND HER DOGS BACK IN FIERY RANT AMID REPORTED BREAKUP
Kelly Osbourne called out Dee Snider after he claimed Ozzy Osbourne did not always write his own music. (Getty Images)
Kelly shared two text-heavy posts, including one directly addressing Snider.

"My father’s legacy as a musician, songwriter, singer and bandleader speaks for itself. His friends, those who worked with him, those who love him, and millions of fans around the world that still continue to buy his records know exactly what he meant what he contributed and what he leaves behind. His legacy will live on eternally," Kelly wrote on the first image.
Kelly Osbourne addressed Dee Snider's comments on her Instagram Stories. (Kelly Osbourne/Instagram)
KELLY OSBOURNE WELCOMES FIRST BABY WITH SID WILSON, SHARON OSBOURNE PRAISES DAUGHTER: 'SO PROUD'
In her next Instagram story, Kelly called Snider’s criticism "spectacularly classless" and argued that he had little basis to speak authoritatively about her father's career and legacy.
"And if Snider wants to invite comparisons between their careers, that comparison is devastating enough on its own," she wrote.
Kelly Osbourne called out Dee Snider directly on her Instagram story. (Kelly Osbourne/Instagram)

Kelly then compared Snider and Ozzy's careers, writing, "Snider had a brief period of mainstream success more than 40 years ago. My father's career spanned nearly six decades — from helping define heavy metal with Black Sabbath to building an extraordinary solo career. His music will continue influencing generations long after all of us are gone."
LIKE WHAT YOU’RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Kelly suggested that Snider’s criticism was an attempt to put himself back into the conversation, while her father’s "name, catalogue and influence" remain globally relevant. She argued that Ozzy’s accomplishments stand on their own, writing, "My father doesn’t need Dee Snider’s approval to establish his place in music history."
Kelly Osbourne fiercely protected her late father, Ozzy Osbourne's, legacy. (Kevin Mazur)

She concluded, "trying to make my father smaller won’t make Dee Snider bigger," arguing that attacking Ozzy’s legacy only draws greater attention to the difference between the two musicians’ careers and lasting cultural impact.
Early Friday morning, Snider returned to X to make it clear that he has "nothing but love for Ozzy."
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER
"He was always lovely to me. @BlackSabbath changed my life! As a songwriter I can be a little touchy about credit and royalties," Snider wrote.
Dee Snider clarified that he has "nothing but love" for Ozzy Osbourne. (Scott Dudelson/Getty Images)
Representatives for Kelly did not respond to Fox News Digital. Snider's representative said the rocker had no further comment.

Ozzy died on July 22, 2025, at 76, just weeks after performing his final concert with Black Sabbath. His death certificate later listed cardiac arrest and coronary artery disease among the causes of his death, with Parkinson’s disease noted as a contributing condition.

title: Halle Berry celebrates 60th birthday in plunging robe with defiant message
summary: Halle Berry marked her 60th birthday with a bold photo slideshow on Instagram, including a romantic shot with fiancé Van Hunt and selfies of her in a robe.
story: ‘The Five’ co-hosts analyze Halle Berry accusing Gov. Gavin Newsom of 'devaluing' women 'in midlife.'
Halle Berry is stepping into her 60s in style.
The "X-Men" actress shared a series of sultry photos on Instagram Thursday, the day before her birthday.
"Today….don’t give a f---!" she captioned the post.
In the photos, Berry posed for the camera in a black robe with large red floral designs and lace along the edges and sleeves.
EMILY RATAJKOWSKI'S SHREDDED RED BIRTHDAY DRESS LEAVES LITTLE TO THE IMAGINATION AT NYC CELEBRATION
Berry posted a series of photos on Instagram to celebrate her 60th birthday. (Halle Berry Instagram)
She wore the robe tied loosely around her waist, creating a plunging neckline that extended down to her belly button and slightly exposed her chest.
Some of the photos show the "Monster's Ball" star indulging in chocolate-covered strawberries, while others show her smiling as she lounged on a daybed.
Berry flaunted her toned body in a loosely tied black robe with lace details. (Halle Berry Instagram)
Fans sang Berry's praises in the comments.
"Not a single f--- left in stock!! Carry on, @halleberry! 🔥" one fan wrote.
Another added, "Why are you so perfect? Ugh 😍😍😍😍😍"

The actress also shared a photo kissing her fiancé, Van Hunt, as the two lounged on a sofa outside.
Berry also shared a photo of her and her fiancé, Van Hunt, locking lips while sitting outside. (Halle Berry Instagram)
On Friday, Berry took to Instagram to thank all her followers for the birthday wishes with a picture of her holding up a card that said, "Happy 60th."

Berry and Hunt began dating during the pandemic, spending four months talking on the phone during quarantine. (Kevin Mazur)

After sparking romance rumors in July 2020, Berry confirmed their relationship in September of that year with an Instagram photo of herself wearing a T-shirt with his name on it and the caption, "now ya know."

Since confirming their romance, the two have often been photographed together on the red carpet and have made frequent appearances on each other's social media accounts. Hunt revealed in June 2025 that he had proposed, but Berry did not publicly confirm their engagement until February 2026.

title: Drea de Matteo says OnlyFans became ‘political statement’ after financial struggles threatened her home
summary: Drea de Matteo says her OnlyFans page was a political statement against Hollywood after COVID vaccine mandates cost her acting roles and her agent.
story: De Matteo told Fox News Digital why she largely stepped away from acting and the entertainment industry as she prepares to launch her new podcast.
"Sopranos" star Drea de Matteo is reflecting on how joining OnlyFans became not only a financial lifeline when she was facing the loss of her home but also an act of defiance against Hollywood.

The 54-year-old actress has previously shared how launching an account on the subscription-based social media platform, which is primarily known for adult content, gave her the ability to financially save her home.

During an appearance Wednesday on Jamie Kennedy's "Hate to Break It to Ya" podcast, de Matteo explained that the platform gave her a way to make a living without relying on the entertainment industry after she became increasingly alienated from Hollywood over her political views and opposition to COVID-19 vaccine mandates.
JAMIE KENNEDY BLASTS LEFT-WING DOUBLE STANDARDS AFTER ‘MAGGOT’ ATTACKS
Drea de Matteo described joining OnlyFans as a "political statement." (Getty Images)
"In some ways, the OnlyFans page was almost like a political statement on my part in a way," she said.
"Oh yeah, get back at the system," Kennedy interjected.
"It was like, ‘F--- you,'" she said. "'I don’t need to work for your f---ing corporation.'"

De Matteo said the income she received from OnlyFans gave her the financial freedom to successfully fund her own entrepreneurial ventures, including her clothing line Ultrafree and her "Ultrafree" podcast.
‘AMERICAN PIE’ ALUM SHANNON ELIZABETH TURNS TO ONLYFANS FOR ‘FRESH START’ AS DIVORCE UNFOLDS
"You launched your OnlyFans to be free," Kennedy said.
"Yes, I did," she replied.
The "Sopranos" star launched an OnlyFans account while she was facing the potential loss of her home.  (Dia Dipasupil/Getty Images)

Despite her success on "The Sopranos," she said she was never as financially secure as people assumed. The actress told Kennedy she had never been particularly career-driven and would often return to acting only when she needed the income.
"I had enough to survive," she said. "I would always go back to work when I knew I needed to put aside a chunk of money for the mortgage."
'MARRIED... WITH CHILDREN' STAR TED MCGINLEY REVEALS HE GETS PENNY RESIDUAL CHECKS FROM HIS HIT TV SHOWS
"I was not — people think I'm made of f---ing money," de Matteo continued. "Everyone sees me coming, they're like, ‘Here comes that rich b---- from "The Sopranos."
"And it's like, no, I'm not at all. In fact, you know, I live a pretty f---ing normal life. I had to do that [OnlyFans] page to get a lien off my house after foreclosure."

She said her ability to work became further limited during the COVID-19 pandemic, when she declined roles she could not take without being vaccinated. She recalled that her agent eventually dropped her after determining there was little work the agency could secure for her if she remained unvaccinated.

The decline in acting income compounded her financial troubles. She said she took a mortgage forbearance during the pandemic, temporarily pausing payments on her home, but later began receiving foreclosure notices. Although she was ultimately able to resolve the foreclosure, she said she was left with a lien on the property.
De Matteo said her OnlyFans is a "fan page" for her character in "The Sopranos." (Anthony Neste/Getty Images)
In August 2023, de Matteo announced on Instagram that she had created an OnlyFans account, sharing a nude photo and saying she would be charging viewers $15 a month for exclusive content.
*NSYNC’S JOEY FATONE NEARLY WENT BANKRUPT AFTER BOY BAND FAME, HAD ELECTRICITY SHUT OFF ON CHRISTMAS
While speaking with Kennedy, she recalled that she immediately received a financial windfall after launching her OnlyFans page.
"I put a picture up, and, within 75 minutes, the lien was paid," she said. "So, that was why I kept the OnlyFans."
"A picture. What type of picture?" Kennedy asked.
"A picture of me in a bikini," she replied.
Later in the conversation, when Kennedy asked about the amount of the lien, de Matteo told him, "That was $75,000."
"I needed more money than that, but that was just for the lien," she added.
"Did you pay your house off?" Kennedy asked, to which she replied, "No, no."
"So, were you making like a hundred G's a month?" he asked.
"Um, I think sometimes I might have," she said.
However, she said earning money from posting photos was not the original reason she created the account.
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
The actress said she made $75,000 within 75 minutes of joining the platform.  (Monica Morgan/WireImage)

"Honestly, we were going to use the Only Fans platform to start a podcast because I was afraid that I'd be censored too much to talk about stuff, you know, just out there in the world," she told Kennedy.
She explained that she initially set up the page as a "placeholder" for the podcast before her financial situation led her to use the platform differently.
The actress also pushed back on assumptions about the type of content she shares on the platform.
"I only got naked once," she said.
She explained that the photo she posted was tied to the launch of her podcast and intended as a protest against geoengineering.
"So, I painted my whole body in protest art and nobody would touch it because it said ‘stop geoengineering,’" she said
She explained that she believes many of her subscribers are drawn to her page because of her role as Adriana La Cerva, her character on "The Sopranos."

"The OnlyFans thing, I always say, it’s Adriana’s fan page because people love her," she said. "I mean, I’ve done a lot of other TV shows, but that’s the TV show people really love. So, you want to see more Adriana, go there, and that’s where I am."
The actress also clarified comments that she previously made about her son's involvement with her OnlyFans page.  (Steve Granitz/WireImage)
During her appearance on the podcast, de Matteo also clarified previous remarks she had made about her teenage son's involvement with helping create content for her page.
In 2024, she made headlines after appearing on "Not Today, Pal," the podcast hosted by her former "Sopranos" co-stars Robert Iler and Jamie-Lynn Sigler.
During the appearance, Iler told her that her then-13-year-old son had said he edited her OnlyFans photos, which she appeared to confirm.
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER
"Oh yeah. He’s like, ‘So, what do you want me to do with the bikini line here?’" she said at the time.
De Matteo shares two children with her ex, Shooter Jennings.
She told Kennedy that the exchange was taken out of context, explaining that her son had edited a single photo of her dressed as a superhero.
De Matteo said her son edited only one photo of her in a superhero costume.  (Paul Archuleta/Getty Images)
Later in the interview, she was more emphatic about what she said was her son's limited involvement, saying he "has nothing to do with the OnlyFans page."
"However, you know, as it was being launched and stuff, they were included in every f---ing step of what I did," she said of her children. "They knew what pictures were going up in the beginning."

De Matteo said both of her children were aware of what she planned to post and that she would ask them whether they were comfortable with it. However, the "Sons of Anarchy" actress maintained that her son did not regularly edit content for the account.
"He can edit anything," she said. "So, no, he's not editing OnlyFans content. He edited one f---ing picture of his mother as a superhero and that's it."
She said the attention surrounding the story ultimately took a toll on her son, who she said was teased by classmates over the reports.
The actress said the controversy also affected her relationship with her son as she tried to help him navigate the backlash.

"What's f---ed up about that entire thing is it caused such a strain, like even between he and I, because I have to be the person to coach him through all these, like, kind of adverse events, but I'm the f---ing reason for it in this particular instance," de Matteo said.
"So, it was really f---ing hard."

title: Muse frontman Matthew Bellamy seeks sole custody of kids in divorce from model wife
summary: Matthew Bellamy filed for divorce from Elle Evans in Los Angeles, seeking full custody of their two children while invoking their prenup on finances.
story: Fox News Flash top entertainment and celebrity headlines are here.
Muse frontman Matthew Bellamy pulled the plug on his marriage to Elle Evans – and asked the court to give him legal and physical custody of their two young children.

Bellamy filed for divorce on Aug. 12 in Los Angeles. He cited irreconcilable differences as he chose to end the marriage after six years. The musician also invoked the couple’s premarital agreement on key financial issues, according to court documents obtained by Fox News Digital.
Bellamy and Evans’ prenup could now take center stage as the couple untangles their finances.
OLIVIA WILDE SPEAKS OUT ABOUT THE EXACT MOMENT SHE KNEW RELATIONSHIP WITH JASON SUDEIKIS WAS OVER

Muse frontman Matthew Bellamy filed for divorce from Elle Evans after six years of marriage and requested legal and physical custody of their two young children. (Kevin Tachman/Getty Images for amfAR)

Bellamy admitted he had "yet to determine the full nature and extent" of their separate assets and obligations and flagged the possibility of additional community property and debts still to be sorted out. Matthew Bellamy cited irreconcilable differences and referenced the couple’s premarital agreement in court documents filed in Los Angeles on Aug. 12. (Kevork Djansezian/Getty Images)

The prenup’s terms remain private, though Matthew Bellamy indicated Elle Evans could receive spousal support while asking that he not receive any. (Jeremy Chan/Getty Images)

title: 'Blue Bloods' star Jennifer Esposito says she walked away from Hollywood after years of rejection and ‘abuse’
summary: Jennifer Esposito reveals the anxiety, abuse concerns, and Hollywood sexism that drove her to mortgage her house to make "Fresh Kills" on her terms.
story: Donnie Wahlberg has been a cast regular on "Blue Bloods" for 14 years.
After years of attempting to meet Hollywood's expectations, Jennifer Esposito reached a breaking point.

During an appearance on Maria Menounos' "Heal Squad" podcast, the "Blue Bloods" alum reflected on the ups and downs she experienced as a young actress and explained why she finally decided to pull the curtain and call it quits on Hollywood.

"I remember, like, the anxiety of trying to be what everyone wanted me to be," Esposito said. "I got a call one time from my manager. I was on this movie, and they were like, ‘Are you happy on set?’ And I was like, ‘What do you mean?’" Esposito recalled. "Like, ‘Oh, the producer called and said, like, you don't really say good morning.’"
'BLUE BLOODS' STAR JENNIFER ESPOSITO SAYS SHE WAS LOCKED IN PSYCH WARD AS HEALTH BATTLE SPIRALED
Jennifer Esposito explains what ultimately led her to leave Hollywood. (FilmMagic)
The criticism caught Esposito off guard, she said.
"I was just like, ‘We're starting at 5 in the morning. I'm just trying to learn my lines, like, just do my job.’ Like, nothing I was doing was right."
Esposito claimed speaking up about more serious concerns presented another problem.
"And then if you ever speak out about, like, any kind of abuse situation, like, you're not supposed to do that," she said. "Like, you don't do that. You know, there's no right step."
ARMIE HAMMER COMPARES HIS HOLLYWOOD EXILE TO BEING CRUCIFIED: 'THE NAILS ARE IN MY HANDS'
The actress also alleged there was a double standard between men and women in Hollywood, and pointed to Armie Hammer making a smooth return back into Hollywood.
The 53-year-old actress recalled years of rejection and abuse of power within Hollywood. (JC Olivera/Getty Images)
Esposito recalled questioning a stunt in which fake glass was supposed to explode in her face, only to feel pressure not to slow down production.

"They were like, ‘We're just going to blow this fake glass in your face,’ and I was just like, ‘I don't know. Is that right?’ ‘Don't hold us up. You're going to hold us up? Oh, you're not going to do it?’"
After years of questioning herself and revisiting her experiences in therapy, Esposito said she eventually realized she couldn't continue down the same path.

"I would write a little, pick it up, put it down, pick it up, put it down, until I got to a point when it was just like one awful experience after another," she said of developing her movie "Fresh Kills" while continuing to work as an actress.
Then came her breaking point.

Esposito says she eventually realized that she was "never the problem." (Getty Images)
"I remember it was around New Year's, and I thought — I was so miserable," Esposito said. "I was really, really miserable, and I thought, ‘OK, I have to quit.’"
Before walking away, however, Esposito said she felt compelled to make "Fresh Kills," the female-centered Mafia drama she would eventually write, direct and star in.
'FIRE COUNTRY' STAR DIANE FARR LEAVES LOS ANGELES AFTER 30 YEARS TO START HER 'THIRD ACT'
"There was this thing in my head: ‘But make "Fresh Kills" first, because then you can end on your terms, and you could finally do what you believe you can do.’"
Esposito said she eventually realized she could no longer wait for Hollywood to give her an opportunity.

"No one's coming. No one's answering your call. No one cares about you complaining. No one cares [that] women should be in more films, and we should have stories from women. No one cares. And if you think you can do it, then do it," she said.
Getting the movie made brought another round of rejection.
Esposito recalled potential backers offering $5 million if she could secure three male stars and said she was also asked if she would step aside for a male director.
The actress moved to Paris nearly three months ago. (WireImage)
After another discouraging pitch, Esposito decided to stop asking others to take a chance on her.
"I remember getting off the Zoom, and I went out to my husband. I was like, ‘I'm mortgaging the house. I'm mortgaging the house.’"
She said the decision came down to betting on herself.

"Why am I asking these people to bet on me?" Esposito recalled thinking. "I get it. You've never seen me direct anything. You don't know. I hear you. So if I'm asking these people to bet on me, I need to bet on me."

The gamble ultimately resulted in "Fresh Kills," allowing Esposito — who officially moved to Paris three months ago — to make the film she wanted before ending that chapter of her career on her own terms.
The "Blue Bloods" alum admits she doesn't recognize the person she is now after leaving Hollywood. (Getty Images)
"I will never doubt my ability again. No matter what anybody says, I know exactly what I'm capable of," she said. "And it was wonderful to be able to give myself that."

"I don't think I have ever had a calm nervous system ever. Like, I'm being honest. Like, my house was crazy, my surroundings growing up were crazy. Then getting into this industry ... I just finally got to the point where I thought, ‘Why do you keep accepting crumbs from every aspect of your life?’"

She later added, "Now being [in Paris] for three months almost, I really don't even recognize the person I am. I noticed myself smiling walking down the street yesterday. I joined a gym and went in the pool. I haven't been in the pool in I don't know how long."

title: Kelly Ripa admits everyday habit led to painful gum surgery
summary: Kelly Ripa revealed her over-brushing caused severe gum recession, forcing a surgery that left the famously chatty talk show host unable to speak.
story: Fox News Flash top entertainment and celebrity headlines are here.
Kelly Ripa’s diligent dental hygiene came back to bite her.

The longtime talk show host revealed her "good-bad habit" of brushing her teeth too much caused severe gum recession, eventually forcing her to undergo surgery that temporarily left the famously chatty TV personality unable to speak.
"I’m an over-brusher," Ripa revealed during an episode of her podcast, "Let's Talk Off Camera," that was recorded before her surgery.
KELLY RIPA'S PAINFUL SURGERY LEAVES HER UNABLE TO SPEAK
Kelly Ripa revealed that a longtime habit led to severe gum recession and surgery. (Dia Dipasupil/WireImage)

"I brush my teeth too much," she explained to her guest, "Survival of the Thickest" creator Michelle Buteau. "It’s a good-bad habit. But I’ve caused gum recession down here specifically, and so they have gotta re-gum my gums."
Buteau complimented Ripa for prioritizing her health, but the talk show host quickly admitted the procedure was long overdue.
"Before you praise me, I was supposed to do it five years ago," Ripa said. "But now, just so you know, the doctor was like, ‘Now, you don’t have the luxury of time.’"
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER
The talk show host said she had delayed the procedure for five years before doctors urged her not to wait. (FilmMagic)
Ripa's surgery led her to miss a handful of live tapings of the morning talk show she hosts with husband Mark Consuelos.
At the time, Consuelos revealed Ripa's lengthy recovery process included not talking while chatting with musician Nick Jonas on "Live with Kelly and Mark."
"Wow. That’s got to be the hardest thing she’s ever done," Jonas joked.
Describing Ripa as "such a great conversationalist," Consuelos hinted he might have been having trouble getting the talk show host to follow doctor's orders.
"I’m trying to keep her to follow the rules, follow the directions," he said.
Kelly Ripa’s recovery temporarily kept the famously chatty star from speaking. (Getty Images)
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Mark Consuelos said the painful procedure was especially notable because Kelly Ripa rarely complains about pain. (Mike Coppola/Getty Images)
As Ripa recovered at home, Consuelos said the toughest part wasn't the pain – it was convincing the famously curious TV host to stop checking on her healing gums and let the procedure do its work.

"Last night she was like, ‘Can you look?’ I’m like, ‘I’m not pulling your lip down,’" Consuelos said. Ripa instead got into position so Consuelos could check without touching her lip. "So I’m down there like, ‘It looks great!’"
The longtime actor said the surgery was especially alarming because Ripa rarely complains about pain, which made the recovery stand out from any previous trip to the dentist.
"Yeah, it’s painful," he told Jonas. "But she famously doesn’t feel pain. When she goes into the dentist, she doesn’t use the novocaine. But this one hurts, so I know it’s bad."

title: Shania Twain confronts longstanding narrative that her music promotes man-hating
summary: Shania Twain told The New York Times that "Man! I Feel Like a Woman!" was never meant to be a feminist message, pushing back on fan interpretation.
story: Shania Twain told Fox News Digital at the 2024 People's Choice Country Awards that she's embracing the "evolution of country music."
Shania Twain set the record straight after decades of her biggest hits being embraced as feminist anthems — insisting she was never out to bash men.

Twain's influence has stretched far beyond country music, with some of today's biggest stars crediting her as an inspiration. When Harry Styles brought the Canadian singer onstage at Coachella in 2022, he revealed that her music had been part of his life since childhood. "In the car with my mother as a child, this lady taught me to sing. She also taught me that men are trash," Styles said while introducing Twain.
But Twain doesn't exactly remember delivering that second lesson.
"I didn’t ever say that," Twain recently told The New York Times.
SHANIA TWAIN SPEAKS OUT ABOUT THE 'UNHEALTHY' LENGTHS SHE WENT TO STAY THIN
Shania Twain said her biggest hits were never intended to promote man-hating. (Debbie Hickey/Getty Images)
Hits like "Man! I Feel Like a Woman!," "That Don't Impress Me Much" and "Any Man of Mine" have long been embraced by fans as female empowerment anthems.
But Twain pushed back on that narrative.
"It wasn’t meant to be a feminist message," she told the outlet.

For "Man! I Feel Like a Woman!," Twain noted there is "no anger in it" and she didn't write it from the perspective of "a sexist person." In fact, she wasn't even thinking about men when she wrote the 1999 hit.

"I was just owning and celebrating what I think I waited too damn long to celebrate," she said. "People want to celebrate who they are, and what they are, and they don’t want to be criticized for just being themselves. And I think that is a liberty that we all deserve. I certainly waited way too long to give it to myself."
The country-pop icon pushed back on the idea that she set out to bash men in songs like "Man! I Feel Like A Woman." (Kevin Mazur/Getty Images for SiriusXM)
SHANIA TWAIN STRIPS DOWN IN BOLD LOOK TO CELEBRATE 60TH BIRTHDAY
This isn't the first time Twain has pushed back on being labeled a feminist.

"I don’t see myself as a feminist," she told The Times back in June. "I see myself as a very independent thinker and not necessarily because I’m a woman. I am referred to as a feminist. I think I have a lot of feminist points of view because I am so defensive of the vulnerable woman, I really am."
Twain argued that even well-intentioned labels can unnecessarily separate women from men.
"I just feel that I’m strong as a person," she said. "It’s like saying, ‘You look great for your age.’"
Shania Twain said, "Man! I Feel Like a Woman!" was about celebrating herself, not expressing anger. (Getty Images)
In her view, strength and independence shouldn't need a gender qualifier.
"I’m not strong for a woman," Twain explained. "I’m not independent for a woman. I’m not self-sufficient for a woman. I just am a woman. And this falls on boys too."

"It’s, like, ‘Oh, the boy needs less protection than the girl because he’s a boy,'" she added. "That is so not true and it’s not fair. Vulnerable men need just as much protection as vulnerable women."
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER
Shania Twain said she does not define herself by labels, despite aligning with many feminist values. (Jeffrey Mayer/WireImage)

Twain elaborated on her stance, clarifying that her discomfort was with the feminist label itself — shaped by the negativity and confusion she associated with it growing up — rather than its underlying values.

"It’s a tricky word for me, as growing up for so many years the word had so much negativity and confusion around it that I didn’t personally proclaim myself as a feminist, even though when I look at the values and morals of what a feminist is, of course I align with them," she later wrote to The Times.
Before becoming one of country music's biggest stars, Twain said she spent years feeling uncomfortable in her own skin.

"I’ve been very shy about my body from a very young age … to the point where I would not go to the beach in a bathing suit," Twain told "Extra" in 2023. "I would say probably really tortured by it from the age of 10."
Shania Twain said she spent years struggling with body insecurities before finding freedom in embracing her femininity. (Getty Images)
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

The country music star recalled filming the music video for "You're Still the One." She released the ballad in 1998 and noted that the music video allowed her to step outside her daily life at the time.

"I was 30 when I had my first radio hit. … In that video, I’m braless, I’m allowing the platform of stepping out of my daily self into this world of video-making and making decisions that give me this freedom to, like, do things I wouldn’t normally do in my daily life," Twain told the outlet.
Now, Twain said she has found freedom in embracing the femininity she once hid.
The Grammy-winning singer said her early music videos helped her feel liberated and confident in her own skin. (Mathew Tsang/Getty Images)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"I started taking ownership," she told The New York Times, explaining that the music videos she created at the beginning of her career "freed" her. The country-pop star began to embrace her femininity "without feeling shame or feeling like I have to hide it for the sake of my talent."

She explained, "The songs just [became] more and more about that liberation, and about making statements with a smile. Because I wasn’t angry at anyone. I was just, like, ‘Wow, it’s time to celebrate being a woman. This is really, actually great.’"

title: Matthew McConaughey's piece of relationship advice that keeps his marriage to Camila Alves strong
summary: Matthew McConaughey reveals the marriage advice that has kept him and Camila Alves connected through nearly two decades together as a couple.
story: The Academy Award-winning actor tells Fox News Digital the biggest lesson that he's learned in his 14-year marriage to Camila Alves.
Matthew McConaughey is sharing the key to making his marriage work.

During a recent interview with Fox News Digital, the 56-year-old actor spoke about his new film, "The Rivals Of Amziah King," which arrives in theaters on Aug. 14, and the biggest lesson he learned that has contributed to his decades-long marriage.

"You got times where one seems to be affirming and sprinting ahead," he said. "And you got times when somebody else may be a little more insecure or a little more unstable on their feet about their choices and what they're doing."
He explained that when in a relationship, it is important to "try not to get too much of a gap between those two" stages.
Matthew McConaughey shared the biggest lesson he has learned that has helped his marriage. (David Parry/PA Images via Getty Images)
THOMAS RHETT REVEALS WHY HE AND WIFE LAUREN REJECT CELEBRITY PERKS FOR COUNTRY LIFE

"Is there a way to go, 'I'll slow down so you can catch up, or 'You slow down so I can catch up a little bit?'" he added. "Not asking you to not be in the lead because I want you to be in the lead because when the fire's hot, keep it burning. Go, go, go, go, go. But just keep me in arm's length over here. Keep me in arms length."
WATCH: Matthew McConaughey's piece of relationship advice that keeps his marriage to Camila Alves strong
McConaughey and Camila Alves got married in June 2012, six years after they first met in a nightclub in West Hollywood in 2006.
Over the course of their relationship, the couple has welcomed three kids together; sons Levi, 18, and Livingston, 13, and daughter Vida, 16.

In his new film, also starring Kurt Russell and Cole Sprouse, the "Dallas Buyers Club" star plays Amziah King, a musician, beekeeper and pillar in his community in Oklahoma whose life is turned upside down when his former foster daughter returns as he is also dealing with threats to his honey business.
Alves and McConaughey share three children together. (Rick Kern/Getty Images)
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER
While the actor grew up in Texas rather than Southeast Oklahoma, he was able to relate to his character in the movie, as "it's got a lot of the same characters in it" as he saw growing up.
WATCH: Matthew McConaughey says new movie characters remind him of people he knew growing up in Texas

"There's a lot of people in a lot of places all across the United States where music is how you communicate, it's how you survive, it's how you keep belief alive, it's how they keep hope alive, because if you look at logic, and you look at the facts every single day, all we got to do is look at the news," he said.

"Oh, that doesn't do a lot for keeping your belief and hope alive. If anything, it puts a damper on it," he added. "So music and belief are like, 'Hey, we're gonna play through the struggle. We're going to sing through it. We're gonna dance through it, we're going to say that any time is a good time to put you in the spotlight and say, you're on, go.'"
McConaughey told Fox News Digital he had the opportunity to play the instruments himself and sing in the film, noting, "singing and playing at the same time is not as easy as I thought."
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
McConaughey plays instruments and sings in his new film. (Robby Klein/Getty Images for IMDb)

The actor shares that "musicality" is important to him in all his roles, saying, "There is a rhythm for every character," and while he always has "a set of djembes in my trailer," he found that when singing and playing at the same time, "my hands couldn't keep up with my mouth."
"It's a very musical character and I actually got to play and sing in this and that was a hell of a lot of fun," he said. "And I had a lot of help from the real musicians that were there."
"The Rivals Of Amziah King" hit theaters on Friday, Aug. 14.
WATCH: Matthew McConaughey reveals surprising challenge he faced while making new movie
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Last week, McConaughey and Alves were photographed meeting Pope Leo XIV at St. Peter’s Basilica in Vatican City.
The actor and his model wife grinned during the moment, which took place during the pope’s weekly general audience.
The actor has been in Italy filming his new Netflix movie "Positano." McConaughey stars in the movie alongside Zoe Saldaña.
The Texas-born movie star has been open about his faith over the years, and has even published a book called "Poems & Prayers" in 2025.
McConaughey told Fox News Digital he felt "a little nicely anxious" about meeting the Pope.

"Yeah, as the man in the world that represents most cleanly the moral aperture and judgment. What an awesome position," he added. "And, you know, the Pope has had different amounts of power through the history of time in politics. There were paintings there where… actually the kings in the past came to kiss the Pope's feet for the blessing, you know what I mean?"
Last week, McConaughey and Alves were photographed meeting Pope Leo XIV at St. Peter’s Basilica in Vatican City. (Simone Risoluti - Vatican Media via Vatican Pool/Getty Images)

The movie star noted that the Pope is still "the moral compass," which he says is "really important, especially... as politics has gained so much power and popularity and has been sort of our fulcrum for which we look at, for almost where our values come from. Politics is part of the values of whether you want to call it religious or not."

"He noted that while there's a separation between church and state, there's still "values of politics" that "need to come down through certain religious aspects, I believe. And they're even built on those in some way. Yeah, I understand law is separate from belief or values, so to speak, but they're always going to be intrinsically aligned and should be in some way," McConaughey said.

"And it's something we're going through now. We're trying to figure out the standards of AI, you know, what are the morals and ethics and the values that we need to set as a standard within AI –  that's becoming this new power and platform and tool in our lives," he said.
When asked what he talked to the Pope about, he said, "That's between he and I."
Lori A. Bashian is an entertainment news writer at Fox News Digital.

title: Julianne Hough flaunts her toned figure in bikinis as she shares snaps from her trip to Sardinia
summary: Julianne Hough shared photos from her Sardinia, Italy, girls trip featuring white string bikini beach moments, cliff jumping and seaside yoga.
story: ‘Dancing with the Stars’ co-host Julianne Hough tells Fox News Digital what she thought about the Taylor Swift-themed night.
Julianne Hough is trading the hustle for a taste of la dolce vita.

The 38-year-old "Dancing with the Stars" co-host shared highlights from an adventurous girls getaway to Sardinia, Italy, where she jumped from cliffs, explored local villages, hit the beach and squeezed in seaside workouts.
In one photo from the getaway, Hough lounged on a beach chair in a white string bikini.
LANDMAN' STAR ALI LARTER SHOWS OFF HER FIT PHYSIQUE IN BARELY-THERE BIKINIS DURING YACHT VACATION IN ITALY
Julianne Hough soaked up the sun in a white string bikini during a getaway to Sardinia, Italy. (Julianne Hough/Instagram)
The dancer leaned back on the chair with one leg bent as she posed near the water. She paired the white string bikini with black sunglasses and a white mesh headscarf over her short blonde hair.
Beachgoers filled the shoreline behind Hough, while yachts floated in the bright blue water farther out.
"Still thinking about Sardinia and how special it was to experience it with my girls @drewdylanlex and @briannacope," Hough wrote on Instagram.
"There’s just something about seeing the world with people you love that makes everything feel a little more alive."
MOLLY SIMS FLAUNTS TONED ABS IN MISMATCHED BIKINI DURING PERFECT BEACH DAY WITH HER KIDS
Hough also showed off another bikini during a quieter moment overlooking the coast.
In the photo, she sat on the edge of a lounge chair beneath a rustic shaded canopy while wearing a dark string bikini with a coordinating wrap tied low around her waist.
Julianne Hough shared a glimpse of the scenic views she enjoyed during her trip. (Julianne Hough/Instagram)
Hough turned toward the water as the secluded setting offered sweeping views of the rocky shoreline and calm sea.
"The beauty, the food, the wildness, the peace… already dreaming about going back to @resort_erica where should we go next and who’s coming?" she wrote.
‘THE MADISON’ STAR ELLE CHAPMAN SAYS 8-MILE HIKES, HORSE RIDES IN MONTANA KEPT HER ‘GROUNDED’
The dancer made time to stay active during the trip, sharing a separate photo of herself practicing yoga on a wooden deck overlooking the water.
Julianne Hough squeezed in a seaside yoga session while embracing a slower pace during her Sardinia getaway. (Julianne Hough/Instagram)
The photo was part of a separate post in which Hough reflected on the slower pace of life she experienced in Sardinia.
"An ode to the nonnas of Sardinia… their sun kissed skin and the sense that they haven’t just spent their lives working but living," she wrote.
Hough admitted the experience had her reconsidering how she balances ambition with enjoying her life away from work.

"And boy, do I feel like the silly American in Europe. I love my work and my ambition, but when I’m older, I’d rather be the grandmother with stories to tell than wonder if I hustled more than I lived.

"Grateful to @hotelcapodorso for reminding me to slow down, breathe the salty air, taste the wine, and watch those stories pass by over an espresso 🤍
"from spa to sea, grazie."
Hough also traded her beachwear for a glamorous look during the getaway.
In another photo, she posed in a strapless coral pink gown with a fitted bodice and voluminous skirt while standing along a picturesque street lined with stone buildings and terracotta roofs.
Julianne Hough traded her beachwear for a colorful dress during her Sardinia getaway. (Julianne Hough/Instagram)
Hough looked down as the flowing skirt swept outward around her, completing the look with a statement gold necklace and strappy heels.
The trip offered Hough some downtime ahead of another busy chapter in her longtime relationship with "Dancing with the Stars."
Hough first joined the competition series as a professional dancer in 2007 and has since served as a judge and co-host.

Julianne Hough has been a longtime fixture on "Dancing with the Stars" as a professional dancer, judge and co-host. (Jamie McCarthy/Getty Images)
Earlier this year, she reflected on the unlikely longevity of the series, which premiered in 2005.
"I mean, this show got turned down so many times at the beginning because people were like, ‘A ballroom dancing show? Like, what? Is that really a thing?’" Hough told People magazine in May.
More than two decades after its debut, Hough said the show's ability to remain true to its roots has helped it endure.

"To see that it's been around not only just, like, survived 20 years, but is now thriving more than it ever has, it just goes to show that, like, when you stay in authenticity and integrity of what this show is — which is craftsmanship, just rooting for people to grow and succeed, and go on the journey of transformation, and keep that family experience — that's timeless," she told the outlet.

MEGHAN MARKLE’S ROYAL EXIT HAD WARNING SIGNS YEARS EARLIER, VETERAN CORRESPONDENT REVEALS

title: Matthew McConaughey gives update on rumored 'Yellowstone' spin-off series, years after reports first surfaced
summary: Matthew McConaughy says his conversations with Taylor Sheridan about a "Yellowstone" spin-off are ongoing but confirms nothing is officially real yet.
story: Matthew McConaughey told Fox News Digital that he likes to have a good time with his wife.
Matthew McConaughey is clearing the air about his rumored "Yellowstone" spin-off.

During a recent appearance on The Playlist’s "Discourse" podcast, the 56-year-old actor discussed the status of the rumored "Yellowstone" spin-off he was meant to star in, giving fans some hope that they might still see him in that universe.

"No, I mean, it’s not any more of a thing than it was or probably any less of a thing than it was that did hit the headlines there for a while," McConaughey said. "Taylor and I have spoken and have continued to have conversations about what [it could be] and if that would be whatever. But nothing’s real yet."

Rumors of a potential collaboration between McConaughey and Taylor Sheridan first sparked in 2023, when Sheridan was still trying to figure out the end of "Yellowstone" and whether its star, Kevin Costner, would return.
McConaughey gave his fans an update on his rumored collaboration with Taylor Sheridan. (PG/Bauer-Griffin/GC Images)
LIONESS STAR MICHAEL KELLY CALLS TAYLOR SHERIDAN 'ONE OF THE GREATEST STORYTELLERS' IN ENTERTAINMENT
During the gap between the first half of the show's final season and the second, rumors began swirling that McConaughey and Sheridan were in talks for a potential spin-off of the show.
Sheridan told The Hollywood Reporter in June 2023 that McConaughey "seems like a natural fit."

"We had a few conversations over the years and spitballed a few ideas," Sheridan said. "Then he started watching 'Yellowstone' and responded to it. He was like, ‘I want to do that.’ And by ‘that’ he meant diving into a raw world clashing up against the modern world. And then I said, ‘Buddy, that we can do.’"
"Yellowstone" aired its series finale in December 2024 without Costner, Sheridan giving his character an off-screen death.
Costner did not return to film the second half of Season 5 of "Yellowstone." (Kevin Mazur/Getty Images for Airbnb)
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

It was announced in August 2024 that two of the show's stars, Cole Hauser and Kelly Reilly, who played Beth Dutton and Rip Wheeler, would star in their own spin-off series, "Dutton Ranch," which saw the two characters leave Montana to start fresh in Texas.
While this show is an extension of the "Yellowstone" universe, Sheridan stepped away from the writers' room during the first season, although he is still an executive producer.

"There were challenges, you know?" Hauser told Film Inside NYC in July. "Not having Taylor [Sheridan] there for us to really kind of be able to work with these new writers, these new directors, these people ... everything had changed."

Kelly Reilly as Beth Dutton and Cole Hauser as Rip Wheeler in "Dutton Ranch." (Lo Smith/Paramount+)

In the end, Hauser said he is "proud of what we accomplished" on the show, crediting everyone on set for having to "figure out on our feet how to really perform and tell a story," noting, "I look forward to doing it again."
