title: Watch ‘Frozen 3’ Stars Kristen Bell And Idina Menzel’s Striking Performance at Disney Fan Event
summary: Just. Wow. The stars of the “Frozen 3,” the third installment of the successful Disney franchise, capped off the D23 expo in Anaheim, California on Aug. 14 with a breathtaking performance.
story: Just. Wow.
The stars of the “Frozen 3,” the third installment of the successful Disney franchise, capped off the D23 expo in Anaheim, California on Aug. 14 with a breathtaking performance.

During the event, in which Disney shared several updates and details about their upcoming projects, Kristen Bell and Idina Menzel, who voice Anna and Elsa respectively, sang a new version of “Frozen Heart.” And the two absolutely crushed it.

The event showcased several different upcoming projects including the live-action “Tangled” and “The Bluey Movie.” During the event’s grand finale, the “Frozen” portion of the event, Josh Gad, who voices lovable snowman Olaf, performed a new song entitled “Ooooh, Samantha,” in honor of his character’s first crush.

Disney also revealed that in the upcoming film, which will hit theaters on November 24, 2027, Anna is getting married to Kristoff, voiced by Jonathan Groff. There’s also a new villain, whose powers are said to rival that of Anna’s. The updates come almost seven years since “Frozen 2” came out.
The fan expo this year was filled with developments. During the Marvel portion of the showcase, fans got a peek at the stars of the upcoming “X-Men” film, that’s scheduled for a 2028 debut.

In addition to Sadie Sink as Jean Grey, Marvel introduced Kit Connor as Scott Summers, Christopher Abbott as Professor Charles Xavier, Samara Weaving as Emma Frost, Inde Navarrette as Rogue and Maya Boyd as Storm. Adam Driver will play villainous geneticist Mister Sinister.

“Kevin and I had been talking for years about my joining the Marvel Cinematic Universe, and I think we finally found the perfect film,” Driver told the audience through a video that played at the event.

title: 1st Look at ‘Tangled’ Live-Action Film Shows Kathryn Hahn as A Chilling Mother Gothel
summary: Fans just got a first peek at the upcoming live-action “Tangled” film and Kathryn Hahn in particular blew their minds.
story: Fans just got a first peek at the upcoming live-action “Tangled” film and one actor in particular blew their minds.

During the showcase at Disney’s D23 convention in Anaheim, California on Aug. 14, audience members were able to see a teaser for the film, which will be a retelling of the 2010 Disney animated movie. The clip included a look at Teagan Croft in the lead role of Rapunzel as well as Kathryn Hahn as the villain Mother Gothel. And people truly cannot handle Hahn’s sinister look.
The film, which is based on the German fairy tale “Rapunzel” by the Brothers Grimm, is slated to hit theaters March 31, 2028, Disney announced at the event.
In the teaser, Croft’s Rapunzel appears on screen with her lengthy, blonde locks. Hahn’s Mother Gothel is later heard, calling out to Rapunzel, before dissolving into wicked laughter.
Mother truly couldn’t be more chilling.

Hahn — who’s cemented her status as a queen of all things spooky due to her performance as witch Agatha Harkness in Marvel’s Cinematic Universe — received quite the reception from the audience in addition to social media users, who have described her casting as “perfect.”
“shes serving the exact unhinged maternal menace that made the original gothel iconic,” one X user said.
Another fan said that Hahn was “BORN FOR THIS.”

The “Tangled” segment of the showcase also featured a message from Croft and Milo Manheim, who plays the dashing Flynn Rider. The pair, who filmed the message from Spain, shared some views from  their shooting locations in the country, including monasteries and cathedrals.
In an interview with E! News, Hahn gushed over the experience on the film.
“The cast is so delicious,” Hahn said. “I can’t believe I’m singing and dancing at this stage in my life.”

The D23 event also included several other big moments. Disney debuted a first look at “The Bluey Movie,” based on the beloved kids’ television show. The movie is slated to hit theaters on August 6, 2027.

Fans also got to see the stars of the upcoming “X-Men” film, that’s scheduled for a 2028 debut. In addition to Sadie Sink as Jean Grey, Marvel introduced Kit Connor as Scott Summers, Christopher Abbott as Professor Charles Xavier, Samara Weaving as Emma Frost, Inde Navarrette as Rogue and Maya Boyd as Storm. Adam Driver will play villainous geneticist Mister Sinister.

title: Anne Hathaway Thinks All Movies Where A Dog Dies Should Get This Rating
summary: Anne Hathaway has some thoughts that are likely to make most dog lovers say, “Amen!” The actor, who stars in the sci-fi thriller “The End Of Oak Street,” told Complex in an Aug. 13 clip that films that kill off dogs should “automatically be rated R.” “Doesn’t matter if anybody curses.
story: Anne Hathaway has some thoughts that are likely to make most dog lovers say, “Amen!”
The actor, who stars in the sci-fi thriller “The End Of Oak Street,” told Complex in an Aug. 13 clip that films that kill off dogs should “automatically be rated R.”
“Doesn’t matter if anybody curses. It doesn’t matter if there’s violence,” Hathaway told the outlet. “If a dog dies — R-rated.”

The film, which was released in theaters Aug. 14, revolves around the Platt family, who are thrown into chaos after a cosmic event transports them into prehistoric times. Hathaway, who plays matriarch Denise Platt, assured viewers that the family dog in the film, Starbuck, does not die as many had feared. And no, the movie isn’t rated-R — it is in fact a PG-13 flick.
“We break rules in this movie,” Hathaway told Complex. “That might not be one of them.”

Hathaway said she’s seen the concern from fans for Starbuck. And she suspects that the fears around his potential death have to do with movies that have “traumatized” viewers like the 2014 film “John Wick,” during which a beloved beagle named Daisy meets a horrible end amid a home invasion.

“I think everybody’s so traumatized by ‘John Wick’ because I’ve been seeing those too,”  Hathaway said of the concern for Starbuck. “Like, ‘They better not kill the dog!’ I’m like, which movies are out there killing dogs that everybody is so scared that they’re just casually doing it in movies now?”

Currently, movies can fall under an R-rating if they include violence that is graphic in nature. This includes those that show varying amounts of blood or gore, torture and more. Injuries are usually evident as well. PG-13 films, on the other hand, can include violence that has some realistic qualities. However, the violence “will not be both realistic and pervasive or extreme.” The ratings do not specify the types of victims of the acts of violence.
Dog lovers seemed to agree with Hathaway’s take.
“The one time I don’t mind spoilers. If the dog dies I’m not watching the movie no matter the good reviews,” the Instagram user said.
Another said that “There’s no reason to kill a dog in a movie ever.”

title: Matthew McConaughey Shares How His Mom Reacted When He Felt ‘Insecure, Not Confident’
summary: Matthew McConaughey reveals why “The Rivals of Amziah King” inspired his return to the big screen, how it reflects his own upbringing and which of his movies is his favorite.
story: When the camera cuts, the interview isn’t over. With “Cut for Time,” TODAY.com asks the questions our anchors couldn’t get to on-air.
If you’ve ever wondered what it’s like to stand a foot from Matthew McConaughey, his steady gaze locked intently on yours, it is, in a word, intoxicating.
His charisma is an 11 out of 10, and the Oscar winner somehow manages to make you feel that, despite standing in the crowded room to the side of Studio 1A, you’re the only person that exists.

Maybe that’s why McConaughey has an Academy Award in the first place. Or, maybe it’s because the 56-year-old is genuinely invested. Either way, he seems utterly present in the moment, even if that moment is answering a few hurried questions about his latest movie, Andrew Patterson’s indie film “The Rivals of Amziah King.”

In recent years, McConaughey has stepped back from acting to to focus on other things, including his best-selling memoir, “Greenlights,” as well as a pair of other books: a collection of prayers and poems and a children’s picture book.
But it’s the title role in Patterson’s feature, an ambitious Southern drama, thriller, father-daughter beekeeping tale, that’s inspired his return.

The “Dallas Buyers Club” actor explains to TODAY.com why this is the role that brought him back to the big screen and how it mirrors his own upbringing. Finally, before heading off to the airport, McConaughey reveals which of his movies he counts among his favorites and why.
And, in case you’re wondering, yes, his eyes really are that blue.
This interview has been lightly edited for clarity.

On a script level, it was the most original, in particular, play, space and time and character I’ve read in a long time. I’d seen the director Andrew Patterson’s first film “The Vast of Night,” an independent film they made for less than $1 million dollars. I was like, “Oh, this guy wrote this. He’s got control of the story. He’s got control of the camera and it’s good acting. Story well told.”
The character, Amziah, I was like, “Oh, OK, this is a guy who is a giver of belonging. He’s a guy who pulls people who are on the outskirts to the center of the circle, shines a light on them.”

That reminded me a little bit about how I grew up. When me or one of my brothers would be feeling insecure, not confident about something, my mom, especially, would just bring us in, hoist us literally up in the air and celebrate us to an extent to where we got out of our head and believed we were worth whatever we’re worth. And then, we celebrated.

At the same time, if one of me and my brothers came in and sort of thought we were the cock of the walk and had everything figured out, nobody could touch our stuff ... my family is very good about finding your Achilles heel and popping you until you admitted you were kind of full of BS, and you cried uncle.
And then as soon as you cried uncle, they’d do the same thing: Lift you up, celebrate you and say, “There you are. Welcome back.”

This story is a great father-daughter love story — foster daughter with a foster father — and a story about all the underdogs out there. This is a guy, Amziah, who brings the outcast in and says, “You have family here. I’m going to bet on you. I’m going to bet on the best of you. All you’ve got to do is be yourself.”

So, it’s a love story and the love at the center of it is a father and foster daughter coming back together. Basically the fable is Amziah is shepherding her from a princess to a queen, which she literally becomes towards the end, which is something that we all want to do with our kids in a way, right?

And also, without giving the story away, he leaves her something to shepherd herself. There comes a time where we have to, whatever we leave our children, when we go, “I’m not going to be there. You take that.” And that’s a beautiful, beautiful, beautiful thing.

I’m happy to say, besides two films — and I made over 55 — besides two, every one I’ve done, the last one I did was my favorite. Now, every one I do, when I’m doing it, I’m fully convinced that it is my first and could easily be my last, and I’m cool with that.
Because it’s that precious. It’s that: this is it. Doesn’t matter if this is the last one. Oh, this is the first one? Ah, finally. And, it could be the last one. Great. Let’s go out on this one.

title: Halle Berry Celebrates Turning 60 With Steamy Pics That Prove She’s Ageless
summary: Halle Berry is celebrating her milestone 60th birthday with some sexy snaps that prove she’s ageless.
story: Halle Berry is celebrating her milestone 60th birthday with some sexy snaps that prove she’s ageless.
Ahead of her special day, the Oscar-winning actor uploaded a series of steamy pictures to Instagram that showed her spending time with beau Van Hunt.

While donning a lace-trimmed red and black robe and seemingly nothing else, Berry posed for the camera as she enjoyed a day in the sun filled with chocolate-covered strawberries and what looked to be a mimosa.
The post also included a selfie that revealed some of her skincare products and a sweet picture of her sharing a kiss with Hunt while she held a peach in her hand.
“Today….don’t give a f—!” she cheekily captioned the seductive slideshow.
On her actual birthday, Aug. 14, Berry shared a selfie of her smiling widely as she wore oversized white sunglasses and held a card that read, “Happy 60th.”
“Thank you from my (heart) for all the birthday love and well wishes. I’m grateful to still be here!!” she told fans in the caption.
Celebrity friends, like Jamie Foxx, Nia Long, Busta Rhymes, Arsenio Hall and more, wished her a happy birthday and left compliments in the comments.
Prior to her birthday, Berry stopped by TODAY with Jenna & Sheinelle last month and revealed how she felt about entering the next decade of her life.
“Great, because, you know, the opposite would be tragic if I weren’t here,” she told Jenna Bush Hager and Sheinelle Jones about her then-upcoming birthday.
Still, she said she wasn’t feeling how she expected to at this point in her life.
“I feel different than I thought I would feel at 60. What is 60? What is age anymore? It’s a feeling,” she explained.

The “Monster’s Ball” star continued, “I feel stronger, smarter, wiser, more myself, more in control. I’m the best version of myself at this time in my life and I am so glad that I’m still here and healthy.”

During their chat, Berry also reflected on working in Hollywood and making movies for 35 years. She said she is appreciative she still gets the opportunity to tell stories that matter to her while also balancing being a mom and taking time for herself.
“I’m still alive in it. I haven’t gone off into the sunset. I haven’t fallen off. I’m still here doing it on my own terms,” she proudly shared.
She added that she finished shooting a movie called “Fleur,” which allowed her to say “what I want to say for a middle-aged woman.” The thriller is currently in post production, per IMDb.
Berry noted that her current slate of projects are reflective of topics that are particularly meaningful to her.

“I am all about women’s health and female empowerment right now and aging gracefully, not turning ourselves into a monster, but staying who we are and knowing that (it) is a privilege to age,” she said.
Berry shared that she wants women to realize “that we are more than this shell.”
“The real good is what’s come from our life experience,” she concluded.

title: ‘The End of Oak Street’ Ending Is Truly Unexpected. Here’s What Happens
summary: Does the Platt family make it out alive in “The End of Oak Street”? Read TODAY.com’s breakdown of the final act of the Anne Hathaway sci-fi movie.
story: Warning: Spoilers for “The End of Oak Street” below.
Since the ‘90s, the “Jurassic Park” franchise has been the staple for dinosaur-related adventure films. But “The End of Oak Street” is ready to add itself to the conversation.

The new science fiction film, directed and written by David Robert Mitchell and produced by J.J. Abrams, opens on a busy street in a quiet and friendly suburban neighborhood where families are enjoying a block party. There, the Platt family is introduced, led by Anne Hathaway’s Denise and Ewan McGregor’s Greg and their two children Audrey (Maisy Stella) and Brian (Christian Convery). But after a strange cosmic event, the Platts and the rest of their neighbors awaken to find that their street has been transported to the Mesozoic Era.

The trailers for “The End of Oak Street,” now playing in theaters, showed glimpses of some of the terrifying dinosaurs the family must evade as they fight for their survival. However, the flick kept its scariest moments and creatures hidden until fans could see them on the big screen. And the 100-minute movie wastes little time before insatiable Tyrannosauruses, Pterodactyls and a Titanoboa (a frightening and massive snake) descend upon the neighborhood and its startled residents.
The Platt family, each facing personal conflicts, must come together and figure out how they traveled to the past, and how they can return to their old lives.
Do they make it out alive? Read on for a breakdown of how the final act of “The End of Oak Street” concludes.
How Did Oak Street Travel to the Past?

After Denise and Greg encounter their first velociraptor, confirming something unusual has happened to their neighborhood, they inform their children that they need to stay inside until they develop a more long-term plan.

They pull up floorboards, rip off cabinet doors and use other wooded parts of their home to board up the windows and doors. But Brian is visibly concerned about the missing family dog, Starbuck. The adorable Australian cattle dog disappeared after the first wave of cosmic events, including a blinding light and an ear-piercing noise, alerted the family that something was amiss.

As the four of them theorize what happened, Audrey suggests that some type of tremor in the universe created a time portal that sent their ‘80s neighborhood back in time, and in turn possibly transported prehistoric creatures to the future.

Meanwhile, Denise and Greg, whose marital struggles were revealed at the start of the movie, continue to argue about their relationship. He confesses that he was fired from his job weeks ago and has been keeping it a secret by delivering pizzas to make money. He also calls Denise out for not being forthcoming — she has been writing a novel in which the main character dreams of fleeing her home life and keeps a suitcase packed in case she decides to run away.

One day, Brian hears Starbuck barking outside. He leaves the house through his bedroom window and chases after him. Audrey soon realizes her brother is missing and also ventures into the dangerous, humid environment. Denise and Greg shortly follow.
Does the Platt Family Survive ‘The End of Oak Street’?

While looking for their children, Denise and Greg enter a house. Inside, they discover a floating sphere that they believe could return them to their normal timeline. But they take too long to decide if they should jump into the portal and it disappears.
Elsewhere, Brian and Audrey reunite and invite a newcomer to the neighborhood named Jeannette (Jordan Alexa Davis), whose parents have died, to join them.

The trio find Denise and Greg, but their sweet family moment is interrupted when a T-Rex sneaks up on them. Everyone splits up and tries to defend themselves, Denise with a rifle, Greg with a sledgehammer and Brian with his bow and arrows.

The T-Rex chases Denise onto a porch and traps her. She screams for help and Greg comes to her rescue. He whacks the dinosaur with his sledgehammer, which appears to momentarily disorient the creature. But the T-Rex swiftly regains its strength. The dinosaur tosses Greg into the air and slams him into the ground, snapping his leg in half. Greg cries out in pain before the T-Rex devours him in front of a stunned Denise.
How Does ‘The End of Oak Street’ End?

Determined to keep her children and Jeannette alive, Denise searches for a way out of the neighborhood. She spots another portal and leads the teens to the house where it is floating. They must climb on top of the roof to reach it.

When they arrive, they see the portal is flashing, meaning they have to time their jumps precisely to pass through to another dimension. A fearless Jeannette goes first and makes it through. Brian goes next and misses the portal, falling onto the ground and injuring his leg. A dinosaur attacks him, but Starbuck comes to his rescue. Denise and Aubrey then help Brian and Starbuck reach the roof again. This time, everyone jumps together.

The Platts make it through the portal and land in a pool some time during the night. The homeowner exits her house and informs the family that they are still in 1982 (the first time the film reveals the setting). However, this timeline is taking place minutes before the first cosmic event occurred.

Denise makes a mysterious call at a nearby payphone and tells her children to wait. Greg then arrives at the home to deliver a pizza. The family embraces and Greg and Denise share a kiss. They all watch from a hill as their street travels through time and is replaced by prehistoric creatures. But Denise was able to warn some of her neighbors about the event ahead of time and save them.

Through a news report shown on a television screen, we learn that Denise became an author and wrote about her experience in a book titled “The End of Oak Street.” We also see footage of the U.S. military protecting citizens from the dinosaurs as Denise’s warnings allowed them to be prepared.
The movie ends with the Platts enjoying a backyard barbecue with the real Jeannette, a clone of Jeannette from the new timeline and her parents.

title: After Hospital Stay Broke A Boy’s Duolingo Streak, App Came Through With A Sweet Gesture
summary: A Duolingo user lost his learning streak on the app after a hospital stay. Then, his parent stepped in to get it restored.
story: When a young Duolingo user lost his learning streak on the app due to some medical issues, the app stepped in to keep his winning record going strong.

A user on X, who goes by the handle @762cayuga, shared on the app Aug. 11 that her son had been “unexpectedly hospitalized,” causing him to lose a streak that had he’d held down for more than 300 days, and reached out for an assist.
For those unfamiliar with Duolingo, a streak, which is represented by a flame icon, signifies the number of consecutive days that a user has completed a lesson on Duolingo.
“Any chance you can help a little Duo fan out?” the parent asked on X. “He’s home and recovering, but heartbroken about losing his streak. Any chance some Duo magic can restore it?”
The app responded on the social media platform and by the next morning, the young user was back to continuing his streak, the company confirmed.
“Let’s get that streak going again,” the company responded to the parent on X.

A spokesperson for Duolingo tells TODAY.com that the 10-year-old was quite the enthusiastic user, learning chess, music, Spanish and math on the app. In order to keep the streak going, the spokesperson adds, a user just needs to complete a lesson in any Duolingo course. So the boy’s streak wasn’t necessarily tied to any one subject, however the spokesperson shares that the child has been most active with chess.

In addition to the streak restoration, Duolingo also threw in some gems, the app’s own form of virtual currency, and a streak shield, which learners can use to protect their streak for up to seven days.
The move has received an outpouring of attention, including much love from some internet users who know just how crushing it can feel to lose a long-held streak.
“Seeing this tweet right after my husband finished his morning lesson,” one user wrote. “He takes his streaks seriously too! Hope they are able to restore your son’s and glad he’s on the mend”

Not everyone received empathy from Duolingo’s infamously sassy owl mascot. After one user asked for their streak to be restored after a bad hangover caused a pause in practice, the app had one thing to say.
“get off my page,” the app responded on X.

Duolingo streaks have been the stuff of obsession for many app users. In fact, some have been photographed, keeping up their learning streaks in interesting circumstances like while at the club, or on the morning of their wedding day.

title: KATSEYE Says ‘We Stand By Sophia and Manon’ Amid Their Hiatuses: ‘We Ride for Them’
summary: During their TODAY appearance, KATSEYE members Daniela Avanzini, Yoonchae Jeong, Megan Skiendiel and Lara Raj spoke about Sophia LaForteza and Manon Bannerman.
story: Although KATSEYE is currently down two members and performing as a quartet, the girl group is a unified front.
Four members of the Grammy-nominated group — Daniela Avanzini, Yoonchae Jeong, Megan Skiendiel and Lara Raj — performed live on the TODAY Plaza on Aug. 14 as part of the Citi Concert Series.
The group, who sang hits like “Gabriela” and “Pinky Up,” also spoke about Sophia Laforteza and Manon Bannerman, two members who announced hiatuses from the band this year.
Craig Melvin asked, “Two of the group members are not here today: Sophia and Manon. We understand they’re taking care of themselves. Have you been able to talk to them? How are they doing?”
Raj responded, “As KATSEYE, it’s so important to us to always prioritize our well-being. We stand by Sophia and Manon through and through. We ride for them.”
Savannah Guthrie followed up by asking if the group had a message for Laforteza and Bannerman.
“We love you guys so much, always,” Raj said, and Skiendiel, Avanzini and Jeong next to her blew kisses.

While appearing on the 3rd Hour of TODAY, the group discussed their new album, “Wild Hearts,” which explores several themes, including mental health. For Skiendiel, specifically, speaking about the topic on the album was “really important.”

“I think that’s something that a lot of people struggle with, and I think it’s so easy to see us from the outside perspective and be like, ‘Oh my God, they have everything sorted out and figured out.’ But in reality, we’re just a bunch of girls still trying to grow up and grow into ourselves,” she said.
The process of growing up comes with “a lot of battles and fights,” and Skiendiel said we should be able to “embrace and share” them.
“I think it was really important for me to share just my own struggles with mental health,” she added.

Life in the public eye comes with a whole extra set of complications, and Craig was curious to know if there are things Skiendiel wishes she’d known to help herself mentally prepare for global superstardom.
“I think something that I’ve learned is breaks are so important and to treat your body like a temple,” she said.
The performer acknowledged that she and her bandmates have a tendency of being “go, go, go” with their hectic schedules, but said she’s learned to schedule time for rest.
“I think something that’s so important that gets overlooked a lot is just taking the time for yourself and healing from within, but also externally as well,” she said.
Laforteza and Bannerman are doing just that as they take time away from Katseye.
Laforteza announced last week that she was stepping away from the band to prioritize her “mental health and wellness.” Bannerman announced her own hiatus in February.

In a statement on Weverse issued to their fans, known as Eyekons, the group said that Laforteza will be “temporarily unable to participate in upcoming promotional activities” and added that “it is imperative that her mental health and wellness are prioritized.”

“Sophia has been receiving the utmost support, and following thorough consultations with medical professionals, it has been advised that she take dedicated time for extended rest and ongoing care to ensure a full recovery,” the statement continued. “While Sophia herself is eager to perform alongside her members, the health, safety, and long-term well-being of our artists will always remain our highest priority.”
The group said they will monitor Laforteza’s progress and are supporting her from afar.

“We plan to reassess her condition in September and will share a further update with fans at that time. We sincerely appreciate your understanding and continued support for Sophia, and we look forward to her being back with KATSEYE,” they told their fans.
Laforteza penned a separate message on her Instagram story.

She said, in part, “It truly breaks my heart to have to miss out on a lot. You know how much I love being on stage, performing, and sharing these moments with you. Making this decision wasn’t easy, but I’m learning that health has to come first. I’m realizing that if I don’t take care of my mind and body now, I won’t be able to keep doing what I love the most for so long.”
The 23-year-old said she will be cheering on the band as they perform without her.
In February, the group shared on Weverse and their social media platforms that Bannerman was taking a hiatus from the band.

“After open and thoughtful conversations together, we are sharing that Manon will be taking a temporary hiatus from group activities to focus on her health and wellbeing,” the group said in a statement. “We fully support this decision. KATSEYE remains committed to showing up for one another and for the fans who mean everything to us. The group will continue scheduled activities during this time, and we look forward to being together again when the time is right.”
The news came after all members took the stage at the 2026 Grammy Awards, also in February. The sextet was nominated for best new artist and best pop duo/group performance for their song “Gabriela.”

title: ‘Camp Rock 3’ Ending Includes a Sweet Demi Lovato Cameo and New Final Jam Winner
summary: What to know about the “Camp Rock 3” ending, including Jonas Brothers, Demi Lovato’s cameo, who wins the Final Jam.
story: Warning: Spoilers from “Camp Rock 3” below.
Turns out the final jam wasn’t all that final, because camp is back in session with “Camp Rock 3.”
“Camp Rock 3” premiered on Disney Channel Aug. 13, 18 years after the 2008 release of the original, with “Camp Rock 2: The Final Jam” just two years after.

The original musical served as a catapult into stardom for original cast members Demi Lovato and the Jonas Brothers. The fictional camp, meanwhile, has always been a place for similarly aspiring young performers to come together and learn what it takes to be a rocker.
This new reboot inducts rising stars Malachi Barton, Disney’s newest male lead from the popular “Zombies” franchise, and Liamani from “Descendants: Wicked Wonderland.”

“Camp Rock 3” picks up many years after the sequel, with the Jonas Brothers reprising their role as the members of the fictional boy band Connect 3: Shane Gray (Joe Jonas), Jason Gray (Kevin Jonas) and Nate Gray (Nick Jonas). When Connect 3 loses the opening act of their “Reconnected” reunion tour, they turn to the place they went from reluctant campers to pivotal counselors in search of the next greatest voice.
Maria Canals-Barrera reprises her role as Connie Torres, mother to Lovato’s character Mitchie Torres.

Unlike her former co-stars, Lovato was listed solely as an executive producer of the film. However, fans online weren’t so convinced — and the instincts were right! Lovato makes a surprise cameo towards the end of the movie, making for a full-circle moment with both old and new castmates. News of Lovato’s return was revealed Aug. 10 across social media, including a post from the star herself.

“She’s an amazing producer,” Canals-Barrera tells TODAY.com about reuniting with Lovato. “She’s so talented. Even at 15, she just grabbed people’s hearts and they never let her go through all the ups and downs in her life and her success.”
Here’s everything to know about “Camp Rock 3,” from Lovato’s surprise appearance, all the new Disney Channel faces and how the movie expands on the beloved franchise’s legacy.
What Happens In ‘Camp Rock 3’?
“Camp Rock 3” combines nostalgic callbacks to the glory days with the introduction of some new voices.

Comedian and actor Sherry Cola comes in as Lark, Connect 3’s tour manager who has little patience for their brotherly band drama. Competition is always an element of Camp Rock, and when campers are faced with a series of challenges to determine who will open for Connect 3, Lark is roped into judging. Despite being hesitant to spend tour prep time in the woods, the catchy songs grow on her, and the excitement of the contest wins her over.

Barton’s character, Fletch, wears the “bad boy” shoes of Shane Gray, as he mysteriously shows up late to camp in a cop car. Fletch, like Shane, immediately bumps into the outgoing aspiring frontwoman Sage, played by Liamani. The two align on their shared passion for using music as a cathartic means of connectivity during times of uncertainty.

Liamani, 17 — just two years older than Lovato was when she first stepped foot on camp — nearly manifested her leading role in “Camp Rock 3.” Three years ago, during her time on “High School Musical: The Musical: The Series,” she covered Lovato’s iconic ballad “This is Me” from the original film. Sage is the girl who always has a plan, but influenced by the spontaneity of her brother Desi (Hudson Stone), she discovers newfound anchors of confidence and direction.

One of Sage’s discoveries includes an iconic reference to the first “Camp Rock.” Looking for inspiration, Sage stumbles upon Mitchie’s songwriting notebook, left under the floorboards of her cabin. When Connie spots Sage writing her own songs in the notebook, she gives Sage some words of wisdom.

Another familiar Disney Channel face (new to the “Camp Rock” universe) is Milo Manheim, the lead of Disney’s “Zombies” franchise and upcoming star in the live-action “Tangled” movie. Manheim portrays a former camper turned counselor who helps mentor campers through the various workshops and challenges.

Key newbies include Rosie (Lumi Pollack), who seizes the opportunity to break free from her parents’ classical expectations, Cliff (Casey Trotter), who finds friends who let him beat to his own drum, and Callie (Brooklynn Pitts), a dancer who discovers leadership skills as Lark’s assistant.

This summer, Connie trades in her chef coat for the camp director’s desk, and has the difficult job of enforcing a new rule: No phones. Like old times, when the competition turns up the heat, the campers must decide if certain rules are worth being broken and when revenge is necessary.
When Does Demi Lovato Make Her Surprise Cameo?

At first, “Camp Rock 3” seems to focus solely on the return of Connect 3 and Connie. Fans are in luck, however, because by the last 20 minutes of this trilogy film, Mitchie Torres indeed makes an appearance.
Once the five finalists are narrowed down — Sage, Fletch, Rosie, Desi and Cliff — and Final Jam approaches, Mitchie surprises Connie and Connect 3.
“This is their night, not mine,” Mitchie says to Connie about wanting to stay on the sidelines rather than make a big entrance during Final Jam.

Mitchie, who took a break from a tour to witness Final Jam, stays backstage and reminisces with her mom about how much camp still means to so many kids, who, like her, came here to discover their sound and kick off their dreams.

Mitchie also chats with Shane, Jason and Nate, and convinces them they don’t have to pick just one Final Jam winner. The former campers see themselves in these young newcomers, and Mitchie reminds them one of the greatest talents isn’t individual star power, but how artists can help each other shine.
After the announcement that all five campers will get to open for Connect 3 as a group, Mitchie and Shane fans get their moment.
“You think they know what they just got?” Shane asks.
“Not yet,” Mitchie responds. “But they will.”

As the new generation gears up to perform a finale duet of “We Rock” with Connect 3, Sage catches a glimpse of Mitchie, who gives the young (and starstruck) performer a wave and a smile before walking off camera.
Will There Be a ‘Camp Rock 4’?
While there is no major cliffhanger moment, the end of the scene between Lovato and Joe Jonas does leave open the possibility of a future for the franchise.
“So, same time next summer?” Joe Jonas’ character poses, to which Lovato answers back, “You’re on.”
“Camp Rock 3” will stream on Disney+ on Aug. 14.

title: Tony Goldwyn Has the Cutest Response to Becoming a Grandpa
summary: Tony Goldwyn is going to be a grandpa and he couldn’t be happier.
story: Tony Goldwyn is going to be a grandpa and he couldn’t be happier.

The “Scandal” star’s daughter Anna Musky-Goldwyn is expecting her first child with husband Billy Durden. The writer shared the exciting news on her Instagram, along with a slew of photos of her baby bump and sonogram.
“New project, currently (and probably forever) known as Goobey, debuts next month,” she captioned the joint post with Durden, before seemingly confirming it’s a girl. “We expect her to be a hit.”
In the comments section, Goldwyn expressed his excitement for his first grandchild, sharing that he’s already proudly printed out a copy of the sonogram.
“We already have her picture up on the mantle (ultrasounds look good these days),” he wrote, adding a heart-eyes emoji.
Goldwyn’s former “Scandal” co-stars Bellamy Young and Katie Lowes also commented on Musky-Goldwyn’s post.
Young wrote, “I can’t wait to meet Goobey!!!!!!!!!,” along with many red hearts and smiling faces with hearts emoji.
Lowes added, “Aaaaah!!!! Yayayay! Congrats!!!!”
Goldwyn shares Musky-Goldwyn and daughter Tess Goldwyn with wife and production designer Jane Musky. The couple have been married since 1987, welcoming Musky-Goldwyn in 1990 and Tess Goldwyn in 1995.
In a 2019 interview with TODAY, the “Hacks” actor spoke about his then-32-year marriage and shared how he knew Musky was the one.
“Jane is just the most incredible human being that I know,” he said. “I knew when I was 21 when I met her that I’d better hang on because I’ll never come across this again.”
When asked why he thinks they’ve had such a successful and long marriage, he told Hoda Kotb that during difficult times, they would ask each other: “Are you willing to work on this?”
Their response was always, “Yeah.”
He added that “it takes both people to look at each other” and mutually agree to talk things out.

title: Krispy Kreme Launches Pokémon Doughnuts: How to Catch ’Em All
summary: To celebrate the 30th anniversary of Pokémon, Krispy Kreme is releasing six new doughnuts inspired by the franchise’s beloved characters.
story: Krispy Kreme’s latest doughnut collection is giving us a major dose of nostalgia.
To celebrate Pokémon’s 30th anniversary (how is that possible?!), the doughnut chain is releasing six new sweet treats inspired by the franchise’s beloved characters.
On Tuesday, Aug. 18, Krispy Kreme will debut doughnuts featuring Pikachu, Bulbasaur, Charmander, Squirtle and Jigglypuff, plus a bonus Poké Ball Doughnut.

It’s hard to believe that it’s been three decades since kids were first introduced to Ash Ketchum and his adorable sidekick, Pikachu. After Pokémon trading cards debuted in the 1990s, the imaginary universe quickly expanded to a cartoon, merchandise and more.
Ready to learn more about Krispy Kreme’s Pokémon collection?  Here’s everything you need to know in order to catch ’em all:
Customers Can Preorder the Collection This Week
Don’t want to miss out on the sugary, supercharged fun? Krispy Kreme customers can preorder Pokémon doughnuts by the dozen starting Aug. 13.

When the collection officially debuts on Aug. 18, it will be available for a limited time in shops and for pickup/delivery in the chain’s app/website. Customers can purchase the doughnuts individually and by the dozen.
The collection will be available in a custom Pokémon Dozen box at participating shops and a six-pack box in select retailers.
The Doughnuts Look Equally Adorable and Delicious
Krispy Kreme’s Pokémon collection brings several characters to life. Here’s a little bit more about each of the doughnuts:

Bulbasaur Doughnut: This Original Glazed doughnut is dipped in vanilla-flavored icing, topped with frosting then finished off with a Bulbasaur piece.Charmander Doughnut: This unglazed doughnut is coated in chocolate and toasted marshmallow-flavored filling, dipped in orange-colored caramel icing plus red and gold sugar, then topped with a Charmander piece.Squirtle Doughnut: This Original Glazed doughnut features swirls of cotton candy-flavored buttercreme, sugar, nonpareils and a surfing Squirtle piece.Pikachu Doughnut: This unglazed doughnut is full of lemon-flavored Kreme filling, dipped in vanilla icing, then decorated with drizzle, nonpareils and a Pikachu piece.Jigglypuff Doughnut: This Original Glazed doughnut features strawberry-flavored buttercreme, a strawberry-flavored cookie and a Jigglypuff piece.Poké Ball Doughnut: This Original Glazed doughnut features vanilla-flavored icing, red sprinkles and chocolate icing.
Bulbasaur Doughnut: This Original Glazed doughnut is dipped in vanilla-flavored icing, topped with frosting then finished off with a Bulbasaur piece.

Charmander Doughnut: This unglazed doughnut is coated in chocolate and toasted marshmallow-flavored filling, dipped in orange-colored caramel icing plus red and gold sugar, then topped with a Charmander piece.
Squirtle Doughnut: This Original Glazed doughnut features swirls of cotton candy-flavored buttercreme, sugar, nonpareils and a surfing Squirtle piece.
Pikachu Doughnut: This unglazed doughnut is full of lemon-flavored Kreme filling, dipped in vanilla icing, then decorated with drizzle, nonpareils and a Pikachu piece.
Jigglypuff Doughnut: This Original Glazed doughnut features strawberry-flavored buttercreme, a strawberry-flavored cookie and a Jigglypuff piece.
Poké Ball Doughnut: This Original Glazed doughnut features vanilla-flavored icing, red sprinkles and chocolate icing.
Krispy Kreme Is Also Releasing Pokémon Cups

As part of the collection, Krispy Kreme is also debuting special-edition Pokémon cups available in five exclusive Pokémon designs. Each cup will be filled with 10 Original Glazed Gold Dots (aka mini doughnuts).
Krispy Kreme is Giving Out Free Doughnuts on Aug. 22

On Saturday, Aug. 22, Krispy Kreme customers who show up to their participating shops wearing Pokémon attire will score a free Original Glazed Doughnut. The single-use offer is available in shops and at the drive-thru.

title: The Osage Story ‘Little House on the Prairie’ Never Told — Until Now
summary: The Osage people’s story is finally incorporated into Little House on the Prairie thanks to the new movie. Here’s what to know.
story: In 1868, the Drum Creek Treaty pushed the Osage Nation from Kansas to present-day Oklahoma, then known as Indian Territory.

More than 150 years later, roughly 200 people gathered in Pawhuska, Oklahoma to revisit that history. Osage individuals, Netflix producers, actors and cultural and historical consultants filled the Osage Casino and Hotel for a screening of Episode 7 of the streamer’s new adaptation of “Little House on the Prairie,” which dramatizes the treaty’s signing.

Unlike the original stories, Netflix’s new eight-episode adaptation, which premiered July 9, highlights the story of the Osage people, whose land Laura Ingalls Wilder’s family illegally settled on in 1869, and were later pushed off of by the U.S. government.
The series primarily represents the Osage perspective through the fictional Mitchell family, whose storyline runs nearly parallel to the Ingalls family and provides an Indigenous lens on the story.
For the cast and crew who spent months trying to wrestle an erased history onto the screen, earning the Osage Nation’s approval was more important than that of any fan or critic.

The long-awaited verdict arrived when the credits rolled, and the Osage Nation principal chief approached actor Meegwun Fairbrother, who portrays farmer and father William Mitchell in the series. Fairbrother recalls the Chief telling him, “‘This is our stamp of approval. We like it,’” he tells TODAY.com.

Indigenous stories weren’t only left out in the original books and adaptation. In recent years, Wilder’s stories have also been criticized for including depictions of Indigenous people that reflect racial attitudes common among white settlers of the 19th century.

Production sought to strike a delicate balance: accurately portraying the Osage Nation’s fight to stay on their own land while also preserving the heart and “overall sensibility” of Wilder’s tales that drew readers to the stories in the first place, Robert Warrior, an Osage historical consultant and professor of American literature who worked with the show’s creators, tells TODAY.com.
Read on to learn more about the historical moment the series stepped into, and what it was like for the actors to depict Osage culture and history onscreen.
Bringing Osage History to Screen

When the Ingalls family made their famous journey to present-day Kansas, they arrived on land that wasn’t legally open to settlement. But Pa didn’t know that when he arrived, and neither did many of the settlers who showed up to claim land they had been told was available, Warrior explains.

Railroad companies also wanted access to the region, he says, and those economic interests often benefited from encouraging settlers to move into the area before legal questions about land rights were resolved.
The tensions in the region weren’t just between settlers and Indigenous people. Competing claims to land, political power and economic opportunity collided across the territory.

Facing displacement and hostility, Osage people were forced to make difficult decisions about survival, identity and their futures, the historian explains. Roughly 4,500 Osage people ultimately left their homeland and way of life in Kansas, and relocated to Oklahoma, what was then called Indian Territory, Warrior says.

But not all families made the choice to leave. About 19 Osage families chose to remain in Kansas, which is the historical basis for the Mitchell family storyline depicted in Netflix’s series. The few who stayed encountered intense discrimination: two heads of those families were killed by settlers, Warrior says, and nearly all eventually fled Kansas and joined the broader Osage community elsewhere.
Really, one of Warrior’s most important goals in consulting for the show was depicting that Osage people, like the Ingalls family, had their own ambitions, disagreements and family dynamics.
He sought to ensure they were afforded the same depth in the show’s storytelling as settler families.
“They’re not just 4,500 nameless people who are standing in the way of a railroad,” he says. “They are actual real people.”

Bringing complex Osage history, stories and culture to the screen entailed far more than just recreating historical events. Actors spent weeks studying cultural practices, learning the Osage language and building characters grounded in lived experience.
'Little House on the Prairie'

The True Story of Dr. George Tann, the Black Doctor Who Saved the Ingalls Family’s Lives in ‘Little House on the Prairie’See the Cast of the New ‘Little House on the Prairie’ Side-by-Side with the Original
The True Story of Dr. George Tann, the Black Doctor Who Saved the Ingalls Family’s Lives in ‘Little House on the Prairie’
See the Cast of the New ‘Little House on the Prairie’ Side-by-Side with the Original
Stars Meegwun Fairbrother and Alyssa Wapanatâhk Discuss the Roles

Wapanatâhk, who plays White Sun, William Mitchell’s wife, describes the Mitchell family as the “missing puzzle piece” in the “Little House” world, pointing to how Indigenous people existed in Wilder’s world but were largely absent from the franchise’s most famous books and onscreen incarnation.

For Wapanatâhk, the role was an effort of resisting shallow symbolism and insisting on lived detail: bearing the weight of an Osage blanket, understanding the historical dynamic between an Osage husband and wife and learning ordinary dialogue beyond the words in her script to build a “whole life” and “whole story” for White Sun, she tells TODAY.com.
For Wapanatâhk, who is of Cree descent, it was also important to portray an Indigenous marriage built on love, strength and partnership — a dynamic she says is largely underrepresented in media.

“A lot of times in TV and film with Indigenous characters, there’s always this sense of we’re just a part of the story to check the boxes,” she says. “We didn’t get that sense when we were reading this ... we got the sense that they were real people, a real family.”

Fairbrother, who is of Ojibwe descent, approached his role with a similar sense of responsibility. After both actors spent six weeks learning the Osage language, he embedded his learning not just into how he spoke, but how he moved. His goal, he says, was to portray a “4D character.”
“Somebody who laughs, somebody who cries, somebody who’s got conflict, but he’s doing his best to take care of his family and his community,” he says.

That commitment to multidimensionality shaped not only the effort put into the production experience, but also the version of Indigenous life portrayed to “Little House” audiences: complex people, loving families and perspectives that had always been a part of the frontier story, but rarely able to tell their stories in their own words.

title: Maria Canals-Barrera Raised Generations of Disney Channel Kids. This Is Her Story
summary: Maria Canals-Barrera raised a generation of Disney Channel stars and viewers. She speaks to TODAY.com about returning to “Camp Rock 3” and appearing in the series finale of “Wizards Beyond Waverly Place.”
story: Maria Canals-Barrera is a Disney Channel mom that viewers remember fondly.

For generations of tweens who spent their time repeatedly watching the “Camp Rock” movies or episodes of “Wizards of Waverly Place,” Canals-Barrera was a parental figure they trusted. Her roles as Connie Torres, the mom of Mitchie Torres played by Demi Lovato, and as Theresa Russo, the mom of Alex Russo played by Selena Gomez, were pivotal to the storylines and influential in the most subtle ways.

When Alex got scolded, fans took in the lessons Theresa was giving her. When Connie delivered good news to Mitchie, viewers experienced that same excitement. Canals-Barrera was an understated force that brought delight to many families’ screens.
“I feel very blessed to have been part of the two franchises that helped their diamonds, (Selena and Demi), not to mention all the other wonderful kids on our shows,” Canals-Barrera tells TODAY.com.

As time has gone by, Canals-Barrera has always kept “Camp Rock” and “Wizards” close to her heart. She’s back for “Camp Rock 3,” out now, and recently appeared in the finale of the “Wizards” spinoff, “Wizards Beyond Waverly Place.”
‘We Rock On’: Returning to the ‘Camp Rock’ Era
After appearing in 2008’s “Camp Rock” and its sequel, “Camp Rock 2: The Final Jam,” Canals-Barrera made her way back to the summer music camp to film the third movie.
Canals-Barrera noticed a resemblance between the original cast, that included Lovato and the Jonas Brothers, and the new Camp Rockers.
They brought that “same openness to show who they are,” she says. “Everybody had their own individual voice and style.”
The new cast includes Disney Channel stars Liamani and Malachi Barton, as well as Lumi Pollack, Hudson Stone and Casey Trotter.

The premise for “Camp Rock 3” differs a bit from the two previous iterations. This time, campers compete in a Final Jam to become the opening act for Connect 3, the band played by Joe, Kevin and Nick Jonas. Connie has now become director of the camp, guiding the new talent and taking charge.
There’s popular kids and misfits with a variety of artistic talents, new versions of old songs and references to the previous films — including *that* viral dance.

“I think the audience will be able to identify with at least one of the campers in their individual storylines,” Canals-Barrera says. The new cast, she says, has reimagined some of the classic tracks in “brilliant” ways. But the new music is still as danceable and of-the-times as ever. The Jonas Brothers also perform a new track, “Come On Over.”

Lovato also made her return to Camp Rock, but this time taking on an executive producer role. While it had been rumored she would make a surprise appearance, Lovato confirmed her cameo days before the release.
Canals-Barrera continues to feel connected to her on-screen daughter. Thinking of their initial time together, she says she loved working with Lovato.

“She was so easy to love, so easy to root for. Such a sweet, special person. She’s just this beam of light, that megawatt smile, that incredible vocal talent,” she says. “I loved doing my scenes with her.”
Her role as Connie was representative of something deeper: a hard-working parent, a thoughtful human and a leader.

“It wasn’t a thankless parent role, like, ‘Go to bed.’ It was life lessons. It was anchoring them in what the truth is and what matters and believing in themselves and that they are something special and different,” she says.
Her wisdom and love continues in “Camp Rock 3.”
Back to the Magic of ‘Wizards’
“Wizards of Waverly Place” was “like magic, no pun intended,” according to Canals-Barrera.

That spark fueled the show’s success, with an unmatched energy from Gomez’s Alex and a chemistry within the cast. The show’s comedy was witty and sharp, accentuated by Gomez’s delivery. Yet, one of the most memorable moments in the Emmy-winning show is when Theresa comforts Alex after a breakup.
“I know how much it hurts when your heart gets broken, but time will heal it,” Theresa begins, immediately adding, “On the bright side, we’re all really happy to see you have feelings.”

As Theresa continues to console Alex, humor comes through once again, saying the iconic line: “My parenting guide doesn’t have a chapter on what to do when your wizard daughter’s werewolf boyfriend has been in love with your son’s vampire girlfriend for the past 300 years.”

This experience of a parent feeling lost on how to help their kid or a child feeling like nobody understands, is universal. Viewers saw this moment and felt layers of emotions, like the warm hug that Theresa gives Alex to conclude their chat.
The nurturing energy extended beyond the characters she played. Canals-Barrera shares that she also gave motherly advice to the people she worked with, including Gomez.

“She asked me for relationship advice a couple of times during the show. And that was really honoring to me because I play her mom. I’m not her mom,” she says. “So when (Gomez) asked me a couple of times about marriage and stuff, that was really touching to me.”
As years went by and Gomez found love with Benny Blanco, marrying him in 2025, Canals-Barrera did not feel the need to share any more wisdom. “I think she figured it out,” Canals-Barrera says.
Canals-Barrera, who previously shared a video on social media confirming her attendance at Gomez’s wedding, called the event “so beautiful.”
Not only was “Wizards of Waverly Place” a Disney Channel hit, it also received critical acclaim, winning two Emmys for outstanding children’s program in 2009 and 2012.
Canals-Barrera says the show’s success is “because we really loved each other and the Russos really had each other’s back ... That real commitment and that real love makes sitcoms unforgettable.”
Representation On Screen, Motherhood Off Screen
Canals-Barrera has always celebrated her Latin roots. When looking for roles, her focus was to show her many layers.

“I’m American and I have this Cuban heritage ... with all the richness. To me, it was a plus,” she says. “And then you get to Hollywood, and Hollywood puts you in these boxes. I’m like, wait a minute. I’m everything. I’m not just one thing. Let me be everything that I am.”

As Canals-Barrera’s made it to Disney, she says, the “Camp Rock” and “Wizards” castings were organic and based on talent. She explains that there weren’t conversations specifying her characters’ ethnicities.

“It just was,” Canals-Barrera says about her roles, as well as Gomez and Lovato’s, who are of Latino descent. “What I love about it is that these lovely ladies were chosen because of their skill, because of their talent and their uniqueness. And the fact that they’re also of Latino heritage is just icing on the cake.”
She praises Lovato for her “incredible skills,” adding, “She got the part because she can sing like nobody’s business. She’s an amazing, funny and incredible actress.”
Gomez, she says, “is a born talent.” “She was on set knowing her lines, completely emotionally prepared and a singer to boot.”

Playing a mom to teenagers before becoming a mother herself gave Canals-Barrera a glimpse at what could be in her future. However, she quips, “Nothing prepares you for the teen years ... not even Alex Russo.”

The actor became a mom to daughters Bridget and Madeleine while actively working. Married to husband David Barrera since 1999, Canals-Barrera put the idea of becoming a mother to the side because of her career.
But at the age of 36 and a wake-up call from her sister, she and her husband felt ready.

“We had been prepared, emotionally, spiritually. We were married for years already and we wanted to (become parents),” she says, adding, “It was my sister who said, ‘Hello, you don’t have all the time in the world.’”
She recalls thinking “anything can happen in this business” and began to plan a family. “Everything worked out beautifully.”

With her daughters, now 23 and 21, and career on the path that she dreamed of, Canals-Barrera combined her two passions. She’s been able to bring her daughters along for the ride, most recently to the set of “Camp Rock 3.”
With fond memories of her Disney days of past and present, the actor repeatedly expresses her appreciation for her fans.
“I’m just in a state of gratitude, honestly, for having been able to play these awesome roles and be part of two amazing franchises,” she says.

title: Mariska Hargitay Wants Jalen Brunson to Make an ‘SVU’ Cameo
summary: Mariska Hargitay is manifesting the next “Law & Order: Special Victims Unit” guest star.
story: Mariska Hargitay is manifesting the next “Law & Order: Special Victims Unit” guest star.

The actor, who’s preparing to host the Primetime Emmy Awards this September, has had a packed schedule. After wrapping up a weekslong run on Broadway this summer in the starring role of the show “Every Brilliant Thing,” Hargitay has jumped into filming another season of “SVU.” And she’s got her sights set on a cameo from none other than New York Knicks captain Jalen Brunson.

Hargitay, a die-hard Knicks fan who was famously spotted at a number of games during the team’s championship run, hinted at a potential collaboration with the NBA champ Aug. 13, while discussing her latest projects live on TODAY. She took the opportunity to put a big wish into the universe.
“And I’m hoping that we might — don’t tell anyone, but — see (Brunson) on ‘SVU,’” she told TODAY host Savannah Guthrie.
“I won’t tell anyone,” Savannah promised.

Earlier this summer, the actor was spotted sitting courtside next to Taylor Swift at Game 4 of the NBA Finals. Hargitay even changed outfits mid-game since she rushed over to attend the game after wrapping up a Broadway performance.

She has attended many of the team’s games and has even found ways to incorporate her love of the Knicks into her performances.  For instance, during a June performance of “Every Brilliant Thing,” the actor brought a Knicks jersey on stage.

During their chat, Savannah remarked to Hargitay that “everything you’re touching is turning to gold right now, including Jalen Brunson and the Knicks,” referencing the team’s NBA finals win in June, ending a 53-year championship drought.
“That is all super surreal still, all of that, but I’m really thrilled,” Hargitay replied.
Savannah also joked that Hargitay should continue to reveal more tea and hopefully, the actor’s wishes will materialize.
“We’ll have to manifest a few more,” Savannah said. “Let’s cook up some more stuff.”

Hargitay has actually managed to bring up the Knicks and her friendship with Brunson on several occasions. While appearing on TODAY with Jenna & Sheinelle in June, Hargitay referred to Brunson as a “friend” and said he’s “my inspiration.”
“He is so singular and magnificent. He’s a magnificent human,” she said.
When guest co-host Savannah suggested that Brunson should attend Hargitay’s Broadway show, the actor said, “Oh, he told me he’s coming!”
The ‘SVU’ star also sat down with Hoda Kotb for a June episode of her “Making Space” podcast in June and applauded the athlete and his teammates for their performance in the NBA Finals.
“Here, the Knicks have had this profound effect on the city and provided hope, but also the ability to dig deep and all of the things that we learn (like) never give up,” she said.
The actor spoke fondly of Brunson and praised “what he’s done and what he’s taught us and children.”
“So he’s teaching you? Jalen Brunson is teaching you?” Kotb asked.
“Every day,” Hargitay replied.

title: Nicole Kidman Looks Back on Marriage to Tom Cruise and the 3 Words She Told People Who Criticized it
summary: Nicole Kidman is looking back on her 10-year marriage to Tom Cruise and what she said to critics who cautioned her against marrying young.
story: Nicole Kidman is looking back on her 10-year marriage to Tom Cruise and what she said to critics who cautioned her against marrying young.
Speaking to British Vogue for the magazine’s September 2026 issue, Nicole Kidman said the marriage “thrust” her into new levels of fame in her early 20s.

Kidman was 23 when she married Cruise, then 28, in a 1990 ceremony in Telluride, Colorado. The couple met while co-starring in the film “Days of Thunder,” which also came out in 1990. Within five years, they had adopted two children, Isabella and Connor. They co-starred in “Eyes Wide Shut” in 1999.
“Suddenly I was 22, 23 years old and I had this huge movie star husband. But it just seemed completely natural. We just fell madly in love and it was that simple,” she said.
The actor said she received some cautionary advice before the wedding, which she ignored.

“I remember people saying to me, ‘OK, well this is really going to affect your career.’ I’m like, ‘I don’t care. I’m in love. I want to be married,’” Kidman said. “And then I was his ‘wife’ and they were like, ‘See, we told you.’ I’m like, ‘So what? I wasn’t meant to marry the man I love? Of course I’ll throw my career away. I don’t care.’”

Kidman, 59, did not throw her career away in the slightest, going on to win an Academy Award, six Golden Globes, two Emmys, and a BAFTA. This year alone, she’s starring in the sequel to “Practical Magic” and the TV shows “Lioness,” “Scarpetta” and “Margot’s Got Money Troubles.”

Kidman and Cruise shared they were separating in 2001. Kidman went on to marry Keith Urban and have two daughters with him, Sunday Rose and Faith. Last year, Kidman and Urban shared they were splitting after 19 years together.

Kidman has spoken about her relationship with Cruise sparingly. During an interview with New York Magazine for their Women in Power series in 2018, Kidman said she married Cruise for both love and “protection.”

“I got married very young, but it definitely wasn’t power for me — it was protection. I married for love, but being married to an extremely powerful man kept me from being sexually harassed. I would work, but I was still very much cocooned. So when I came out of it at 32, 33, it’s almost like I had to grow up,” she said.

title: New ‘Ted Lasso’ Stars Share Why It’s the ‘Perfect Show’ To Talk Challenges In Women’s Sports
summary: Between its signature cozy moments and laugh-out-loud bits, Season 4 of hit comedy “Ted Lasso” tackles some profoundly honest issues around women in sports.
story: Between its signature cozy moments and laugh-out-loud bits, the newest season of hit comedy “Ted Lasso” tackles some profoundly honest issues around women in sports. And the series’ stars say the medium is ripe for it.

Episode 2, released Aug. 12, introduces viewers to the kooky, eclectic members of Richmond’s women’s soccer team, the Lady Greyhounds. Several of the Season 4 newcomers tell TODAY.com that the show’s foray into the trials and tribulations around building a successful squad exposes some weightier topics like the major inequities that the women are up against. And it does so without “ramming it down the old throat,” says actor Faye Marsay.
“It’s the perfect show to do it because it’s about the underdog,” Marsay, who plays Lizzie, a soccer player and mom who’s juggling both roles, says.

title: Rob Gronkowski Reveals He Played Matchmaker for Julian Edelman at Taylor Swift, Travis Kelce’s Wedding
summary: Rob Gronkowski did his best to help his old New England Patriots teammate Julian Edelman find a love connection at Travis Kelce and Taylor Swift’s wedding.
story: Rob Gronkowski did his best to help his old New England Patriots teammate Julian Edelman find a love connection at Travis Kelce and Taylor Swift’s wedding.
The legendary tight end and current Fox NFL analyst shared on TODAY Aug. 13 that he and girlfriend Camille Kostek took Edelman along to the wedding of the year in July.
The couple tried to facilitate a spark with the single ladies for the former Super Bowl MVP, who was scoping out the star-studded crowd of attendees at New York City’s Madison Square Garden.
“Julian Edelman was the third wheel, so we were kind of looking for some girls for him,” Gronkowski said. “He was going, ‘Who’s that? Is she single?’ I’m like, ‘Go for it, Julian.’
“Camille and I were trying to play matchmaker, but no luck,” he added. “But Julian doesn’t need any luck. He’s a beautiful looking kid.”
While Gronkowski, 37, couldn’t find a potential love interest for Edelman, 40, he did bring his trademark zeal to the dance floor.

“The dance floor energy was top notch, and the wedding was top notch as well,” he said. “You couldn’t have painted a better picture of how the whole wedding went down. There’s no doubt about that. Everyone was on the (dance) floor, there was DJs, there was magicians going.”
It was a mini Patriots reunion, as another one of his former teammates, legendary quarterback Tom Brady, was also in attendance.
Kelce made his first public comments about his wedding during a press conference on Aug. 12 at the Kansas City Chiefs’ training camp.
His reflections came more than a month after the Chiefs star tight end and the global music superstar wed on July 3 in front of a star-studded guest list estimated to include 1,100 attendees.
“It was a fun offseason man,” Kelce said. “The wedding was the best night of my life, and I appreciate everybody who came out and celebrated and had fun with us.”

There have been scant details that have trickled out about the wedding, which isn’t surprising considering attendees were required to sign non-disclosure agreements. Sources told NBC News that the bride and groom, who both wore white, each wrote their own vows in a “secret garden”-themed wedding.

The family has also shared only brief comments on the nuptials. Jason Kelce, Travis Kelce’s brother, said in an interview he “probably cried more at this wedding than I cried at my own wedding, which probably is not acceptable.”

title: Crowd Confused as Lana Del Rey’s ‘National Anthem’ Is Played Instead of ‘The Star-Spangled Banner’
summary: Ahead of a high school football game, a DJ played “National Anthem” by Lana Del Rey instead of the “The Star-Spangled Banner.”
story: In Lana Del Rey we trust.

The crowd at Waipahu High School in Hawaii was left confused when instead of hearing “The Star-Spangled Banner” ahead of their football game, Lana Del Rey’s “National Anthem” was heard through the speakers.
In video shared on TikTok Aug. 7 by user akikokelsa, people in the stands are on their feet anticipating the national anthem. However, that is not what begins playing.
“What’s happening? This is Lana Del Rey,” the person recording the video says, laughing.
Whens someone nearby asks if this is the wrong song, they reply, “Yeah, the song is called ‘National Anthem.’”
After a few seconds, over the loudspeaker, someone is heard asking, “DJ, can we have the national anthem, please?”
The person recording the video continues laughing at the slight mishap, noting that technically the DJ is playing a song titled “National Anthem.”
The comments section was filled with Del Rey fans who praised the user for instantly recognizing the track. Others joked that the singer’s song was the only anthem they stood by.
“No the dj was right the first time,” one person commented, with another adding, “Genuinely the ONLY national anthem I’d proudly stand for.”
“i love how you immediately knew😭 a true fan,” someone wrote, with the user replying, “SINCE 2013 BABYYY.”
“That’s the NATIONAL ANTHEM, no mistakes,” another commented.
Waipahu High School principal Zachary Sheets shared in a statement with NBC News that the DJ “experienced technical difficulties playing the songs.”
“Thankfully, our stadium announcer improvised quickly and led our crowd with a cappella versions of the national anthem and Hawaiʻi Ponoʻī,” he said.

Aside from the unexpected beginning, it was an exciting night for the Waipahu Marauders, who had a 40–17 victory over the defending state champions Campbell Sabers to reclaim the Cane Knife after 22 years.

title: Maria Canals-Barrera Reflects on Selena Gomez’s ‘Beautiful’ Wedding: ‘We All Cried’
summary: Maria Canals-Barrera, who portrayed Selena Gomez’s mom on “Wizards of Waverly Place,” opened up about attending Gomez’s wedding and giving her advice as a kid.
story: Over 20 years ago, Maria Canals-Barrera comforted and shared her motherly advice with generations of Disney Channel viewers and stars, including Selena Gomez.

As Theresa Russo, Canals-Barrera gave words of wisdom to her “Wizards of Waverly Place” daughter Alex Russo, portrayed by Gomez. Her nurturing nature also extended beyond the screen to real life, Canals-Barrera tells TODAY.com.

“She asked me for relationship advice a couple of times during the show,” Canals-Barrera recalls. “And that was really honoring to me because I play her mom. I’m not her mom ... So when (Gomez) asked me a couple of times about marriage and stuff, that was really touching to me.”
The two entertained audiences as mother and daughter for four seasons between 2007 and 2012, a time Canals-Barrera tells TODAY.com she remembers fondly.
So when Canals-Barrera attended Gomez’s wedding to Benny Blanco, she couldn’t help but get emotional. The couple got married in September 2025.
Years later, Canals-Barrera says she didn’t need to give her former on-screen daughter any advice. “Now, at her wedding, I think she figured it out,” she says.

Canals-Barrera posted a video on her Instagram that showed a side-by-side of her with Gomez on “Wizards of Waverly Place” and then at her wedding. Canals-Barrera shares that it was a moving celebration.
“(The wedding) was so beautiful. The vows that they wrote for each other were just so incredible. I mean, we all cried,” she says. “It was really beautiful. So I’m very happy that she found love.”
“She deserves the best and so does he,” she adds. “I wish them the best.”
The two would reunite again in the “Wizards” spinoff, “Wizards Beyond Waverly Place.” Canals-Barrera reprised her role as the Russo matriarch for two episodes, including the Aug. 4 finale.
Reflecting on working with Gomez over the years, she called her “a born talent.”
“She was on set knowing her lines, completely emotionally prepared and a singer to boot,” she says.
Also returning to her role of Connie Torres in “Camp Rock 3,” Canals-Barrera is forever grateful and honored to be the TV mom for many.

“It’s very encouraging as an actor, as a mother in real life, that the mothering moments mean something to (fans),” she says. “Even when it’s not our own mother. It’s very touching to us. The nostalgia vibe that’s happening right now. I’m so grateful to be part of it.”

title: Travis Kelce Breaks Silence on Wedding With Taylor Swift: ‘The Best Night Of My Life’
summary: Travis Kelce, the groom himself, is the latest to break his silence on America’s Royal Wedding between him and “Miss Americana” Taylor Swift.
story: Travis Kelce, the groom himself, is the latest to break his silence on America’s Royal Wedding between him and “Miss Americana” Taylor Swift.

At an Aug. 12 press conference at the Kansas City Chiefs’ training camp practice, Kelce opened up about the family and friends who joined them. The comments come more than a month after the couple wed in front of a star-studded guest list that was estimated to include 1,100 attendees.
“It was a fun offseason man,” Kelce said. “The wedding was the best night of my life, and I appreciate everybody who came out and celebrated and had fun with us.”

Kelce and Swift tied the knot on July 3 at New York City’s iconic Madison Square Garden. Leading up to the big night, camera crews and fans alike lingered between 31st and 33rd Street in Manhattan, hoping to catch even a glimpse of the lovers.
Part of the couple’s security strategy involved losing the paper trail. In addition to NDAs, invitees received their invites electronically, a source who was invited told NBC News.

Since the wedding, few details have emerged about the event of the year. Sources told NBC News that the bride and groom, who both wore white, each wrote their own vows. Sources also said that the theme of the wedding appeared to be a “secret garden”  — fit for the “Speak Now” singer, to whom Kelce proposed while surrounded by flowers.

Kelce is not the first of his family to reveal details from the inside. Sister-in-law Kylie Kelce opened up about the tears Jason Kelce, Travis Kelce’s brother, shed. She said that the show of emotion was probably “more at this wedding than I cried at my own wedding.”

Later during the press conference, Travis Kelce reflected on the significance of having his wedding at the Garden, where some of the biggest names in both sports and music have cemented their legacies.
“MSG, man,” Kelce said before calling out Swift for attending the Knicks Finals — one of the recent iconic events held at the venue — while he was unavailable.
“I always told myself I’d go for a playoff game when the Knicks were rocking, and my wife went when I was stuck in mini camp, so I didn’t get my opportunity to go then,” Kelce said.
Kelce added that it was “kind of cool to be able to live out my childhood dream of being in that venue, the mecca of all sports venues.”
Kelce thanked the venue staff for allowing them to use the space given their request for privacy.
“It was perfect... and the AC was cooking; that was the best part,” he said.
The 36-year-old athlete is looking ahead to the upcoming NFL season.
“It was a crazy night,” Kelce said earlier during the conference. “It was full of a lot of celebration, but it’s football, baby.”

The upcoming NFL season kicks off Aug. 13 with preseason play. The official regular season scheduled to begin Sept. 9 with a Sunday Night Football game between the New England Patriots and the Seattle Seahawks, airing on NBC and Peacock.

title: McDonald’s New Happy Meal Combines Hello Kitty and Godzilla: See the Toys
summary: McDonald’s new Hello Kitty & Friends x Godzilla Happy Meal combines characters from the Sanrio universe with monsters from the “Godzilla” film franchise.
story: McDonald’s is saying hello to not one but two iconic pop culture figures with its latest Happy Meal.
The fast-food chain is launching a new Hello Kitty & Friends x Godzilla Happy Meal, which combines characters from the Sanrio universe with monsters from the iconic “Godzilla” film franchise.
The meals will be available at participating McDonald’s locations nationwide for a limited time starting Aug. 18.
Everyone knows the most important part of a Happy Meal is the toy, and McDonald’s has created eight exclusive collectible toys as part of the collab.

The chain teased its newest Happy Meal on Instagram Aug. 10 by sharing a short clip of Hello Kitty eyeing a Happy Meal in the ocean. But she didn’t look quite like herself and had what appeared to be a monster suit on, complete with a fierce head and tail.
McDonald’s captioned the post, “cute meets kaiju 08.18.”
On Aug. 12, the fast-food chain made things official by sharing a photo of the toys customers can look forward to when they open up their Hello Kitty & Friends x Godzilla Happy Meal.
McDonald’s captioned the post, “cosplaying right into our hearts. Hello Kitty and Friends x Godzilla Happy Meal out 8.18.”
The @snackwire Instagram account gave social media users a closer look at the Happy Meal toys, which include the following characters:

In 2025, McDonald’s also re-created one of its Japanese dipping sauces for U.S. restaurants in a collab with anime series “Jujutsu Kaisen.” The Special Grade Garlic Sauce was inspired by McDonald’s Japan’s Black Garlic Sauce.

title: Meet the All-Civilian Cast of ‘The Traitors: New Blood’

story: NBC has revealed the cast for the first-ever all-civilian season of “The Traitors: New Blood.”

On Aug. 12, the network shared the 22 reality television newbies who fans will see move into the mysterious Scottish Highlands castle and compete to win up to $250,000.
